title: Beyond the AI energy hype? data-center-related establishment growth, electricity demand, and emissions across U.S. states
abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) and data-center infrastructure has raised concerns about growing pressure on electricity systems and the environmental consequences of rising computational demand. This study examines whether the expansion of data-center-related activity is associated with measurable changes in aggregate electricity demand and power-sector emissions across 50 U.S. states from 2010 to 2023. Using a balanced state-level panel and two-way fixed-effects models, data-center expansion is proxied by annual establishment counts, with population-normalized exposure and several alternative specifications used for robustness. The baseline estimates provide no evidence of a positive within-state association between growth in data-center-related establishments and aggregate electricity demand. This finding remains robust to alternative functional forms, population weighting, state-specific trends, lagged exposure, controls for grid investment and population, exclusion of major data-center states, winsorization, and first-difference estimation. Data-center activity is likewise not significantly associated with either total power-sector CO 2 emissions or average generation emissions intensity. These results should not be interpreted as evidence that data centers have no energy or environmental consequences. Rather, they highlight the limitations of annual st…

Triglycerides and ovarian response in diminished ovarian reserve: a two-sample mendelian randomization and clinical mediation study
abstract: Background Diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) impairs assisted reproduction. Whether triglyceride (TG) plays a causal role in ovarian reserve remains unclear. Methods We performed a bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis using female-specific GWAS data to assess causality between metabolic traits and ovarian reserve markers (AMH, FSH). Findings were validated in a retrospective cohort of 8,851 DOR women undergoing their first IVF/ICSI cycle, using mediation analysis to elucidate pathways to oocyte yield. Results MR revealed that genetically predicted TG was causally associated with lower FSH (IVW β=-0.096, FDR = 5.28×10 -5 ), with no evidence of reverse causation. Clinical validation confirmed this association. Mediation analysis uncovered that TG exerted a direct negative effect on oocyte yield, but concurrently lowered FSH, creating a suppression effect that partially counteracted this detriment (indirect effect: β = 0.0073, 95% CI: 0.0029 to 0.0117, p = 0.0021; suppression proportion: 23.6%). TG did not show a causal effect on AMH in MR (IVW OR = 1.035, 95% CI: 0.965-1.111, p = 0.338), and clinical mediation through AMH was not robust. Despite impacting oocyte yield, TG did not independently predict clinical pregnancy or live birth; age and AMH remained dominant. Conclusion This study provides genetic evidence for a causal role of TG in lowering FSH and…

title: Transformational Leadership, Technology Adoption, and Policy Regulation:
abstract: Purpose: This study examines the effects of transformational leadership, technology adoption, and policy regulation on sustainable competitive advantage (SCA), with learning organization as a mediating mechanism, in Indonesian electricity companies navigating the energy transition toward net-zero emissions by 2060. Research Method: A quantitative explanatory design was employed using survey data collected through a Likert-scale questionnaire from 161 professionals in Indonesia’s energy and electricity sectors. The proposed relationships were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with LISREL 8.80. Results and Discussion: The findings indicate that transformational leadership significantly influences technology adoption and policy regulation. Technology adoption demonstrates the strongest direct effect on SCA, accounting for 36%. The results further confirm the mediating roles of technology adoption and learning organization in strengthening the relationships among leadership, policy regulation, and SCA. Implications: Electricity companies should strengthen organizational learning to develop competencies in renewable energy technologies, while policymakers should provide clear regulations, transition roadmaps, and incentives to accelerate sustainable technology adoption. Originality: This study integrates leadership, technology adoption, policy regulation, and organiz…

title: Government use of budget documents in shaping disaster response and accountability narratives: evidence from New Zealand
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how governments construct accountability through post-disaster budget estimates and budget speeches following major earthquakes. It explores how accountability narratives communicate responsibility, collective obligation and credibility within post-disaster budget communications under conditions of uncertainty. Design/methodology/approach Focusing on New Zealand, the study analyses 42 budget estimates and 10 budget speeches issued between 2011 and 2025 that reference earthquake response and recovery. A qualitative narrative analysis is used to identify patterns of individualising accountability (IA), socialising accountability (SA) and impression management, including their hybrid configurations, across policy domains, communicative forums and political orientations. Findings Post-disaster budget narratives are predominantly hybrid. Accountability is most frequently articulated through IA-SA and IA-impression management combinations that integrate personal responsibility, collective obligation and claims of competence and commitment. Hybridisation is most pronounced in budget speeches, while budget estimates retain more differentiated accountability registers. Policy-domain effects are evident: mental health narratives are dominated by IA-centred hybrids embedded within collective care frames; housing narratives rely more heavily on SA and SA-…

Market Reaction to Merger and Acquisition Announcements in China
abstract: Developed-market evidence generally predicts lower acquirer returns when targets are publicly listed, because bidding competition, liquidity, and overpayment transfer more gains to target shareholders. In China, however, a listed target may bundle operating assets with a scarce financing and restructuring platform, disclosure credibility, and regulatory safety. Using China Stock Market & Accounting Research (CSMAR) M&A records and daily returns, this paper studies Chinese A-share listed acquirers. The event-level dataset contains 18,859 announcements and the clean event-study sample contains 12,596 observations. Average market-adjusted cumulative abnormal return (CAR) is 0.76% over [-3,+3] and 1.29% over [-10,+10]. Acquisitions involving listed targets are associated with significantly higher announcement returns across baseline specifications, narrower windows, and market-model returns. In the full model, the target-listed coefficient is 1.27 percentage points for CAR over [-3,+3] and 1.72 percentage points for CAR over [-10,+10]. State-owned acquirers also earn higher conditional returns after firm characteristics, transaction variables, momentum, and fixed effects are controlled for. The evidence supports a platform-acquisition interpretation in which investors price the financing, restructuring, transparency, and regulatory attributes attached to listed targets. The estimat…

title: Integrated bioinformatics identifies RRM2 as a lipid remodeling- and gemcitabine response-related gene in pancreatic cancer
Zolpidem Intoxication Leading to Coma and a Rapid Flumazenil Awakening Response: A Definitive Antidote
abstract: Zolpidem is a new imidazopyridine hypnotic that has a specific action on the central omega-1 receptor subtype and is a non-benzodiazepine hypnotic. A 39-year-old woman with a previous history of depression and living alone presented to our hospital in a coma with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 3 after consuming 25 - 30 zolpidem tablets. Previously, she had been on antidepressants and sedatives, the details of which were unknown. The patient remained on ventilatory support for 36 - 48 hours after conservative management. The decision to start flumazenil (a competitive antagonist at the benzodiazepine binding site on the gamma-aminobutyric acid type A [GABAA] receptor) was made. The patient was started on a low-dose infusion and showed a positive response over the next day. Infusion titration was performed in incremental doses, and there was a complete response as the patient regained consciousness. The patient was extubated after 2 days of infusion and safely discharged from the hospital.
venue: Zolpidem Intoxication Leading to Coma and a Rapid Flumazenil Awakening Response: A Definitive Antidote

title: Dynamic modeling and frequency response characteristic analysis of a heavy boring machine tool post system based on 5-DOF
abstract: Heavy boring machines are essential for high-precision manufacturing in foundational industries, including energy, shipbuilding, metallurgy, aerospace, and heavy machinery. This article presents dynamic modeling and analysis for a heavy boring machine. Based on the theory of vibration mechanics, a fivedegree-of-freedom (5-DOF) dynamic model of the tool holder is proposed. The coupling dynamic model of the boring bar and the tool holder is established based on the Bernoulli beam theory. The frequency response characteristic parameters of the tool post system are obtained. The natural frequencies of the present model are 7.68 Hz, 12.48 Hz, 24.14 Hz, 31.31 Hz, and 41.19 Hz. Finite element method (FEM) simulations show that the natural frequencies of the tool post system are 7.6621 Hz, 12.483 Hz, 24.179 Hz, 31.214 Hz, and 41.268 Hz, with a maximum error of 0.31%. This close agreement further verifies the effectiveness of the theoretical modeling. Using theoretical calculations of the stiffness and damping parameters of each joint of the tool post system, the transient analysis of the first three natural frequencies is carried out by FEM. The deformation of each structure of the tool post system at different frequencies is obtained. At an excitation frequency of 7 Hz, the maximum deformation of the tool holder is 4.8 mm. title: الجاهزية المؤسسية والتشغيلية للاستجابة للتسربات النفطية في البحر الأحمر: دراسة حالة السفينة MV Ruby-mar في المملكة العربية السعودية
abstract: في ظل ندرة الدراسات التي تقيّم الجاهزية المؤسسية لمواجهة التسربات النفطية في بيئات النزاع، هدفت هذه الدراسة إلى تقييم مستوى الجاهزية المؤسسية والتشغيلية لمواجهة أزمات وكوارث التسربات النفطية في البحر الأحمر، بالتطبيق على حالة السفينة (MV Ruby-mar) من منظور المملكة العربية السعودية. واعتمدت الدراسة المنهج المختلط (التتابعي التفسيري)، من خلال استبانة طُبقت على عينة قصدية شملت (104) من خبراء الجهات الحكومية والقطاع الخاص، مدعومة بمقابلات شبه مقننة وزيارة ميدانية للمركز الوطني للرقابة على الالتزام البيئي في جازان. أظهرت النتائج أن تقييمات (88.5%) من أفراد العينة تستند إلى خبرة غير مباشرة. ومع ذلك، جاءت الجاهزية العامة بمستوى مرتفع، بمتوسط (4.04) ووزن نسبي (85%)، فيما بلغ مستوى الوعي العام (82.8%). وأظهر تحليل التباين دلالة إحصائية للتدريب عند مستوى (p≤0.01)، بينما بيّن الانحدار الخطي المتعدد أن الإطار المؤسسي هو الأكثر تأثيرًا في التنبؤ بالجاهزية، حيث فسّر مع بقية المتغيرات (R²=65.5%) من التباين، يليه الوعي بالمخاطر، في حين ظل تأثير التحديات التشغيلية محدودًا. كما كشفت الدراسة عن فجوة بين التخطيط والتنفيذ الميداني، خاصة في التنسيق وتبادل المعلومات اللحظي. وخلصت الدراسة إلى وجود فجوة بين قوة التأطير المؤسسي وكفاءة الأداء العملي، وأوصت بإنشاء منصة رقمية موحدة للإنذار المبكر وتبادل المعلومات، وتنفيذ تمارين محاكاة مشتركة مدعومة بالذكاء الاصطناعي، وتحديث الخطط التشغيلية للقطاع الخاص بما يتوافق مع الخطة الوطنية للاستجابة.

title: Soil-Water-Plant Relations and Growth Response of Curly Lettuce to Integrated Microbial and Reduced Chemical Fertilization
abstract: This study evaluated whether microbial fertilizer combined with a 50% reduction in chemical fertilizers can maintain or improve growth performance of curly lettuce (Lactuca sativa L. var. crispa) under greenhouse conditions. The study was arranged in a completely randomized design with seven treatments and four replications: control without fertilizer application (C), optimum chemical fertilization (OF), three combined treatments consisting of 50% reduced chemical fertilizer plus microbial fertilizer at 5 mL L⁻¹ (RCF_MF5), 10 mL L⁻¹ (RCF_MF10), and 20 mL L⁻¹ (RCF_MF20), and two sole microbial fertilizer treatments at 10 mL L⁻¹ (MF10) and 20 mL L⁻¹ (MF20). Irrigation was applied at approximately four-day intervals by restoring the depleted soil moisture to field capacity based on pot weight. Effectiveness of injury prevention programmes in female team sports: a systematic review and meta-analysis of hierarchical injury outcomes, training dose–response relationships, and adherence
abstract: Objective To quantify the effectiveness of exercise-based injury prevention programmes (IPPs) in female team sports across overall, lower-limb, and site-specific injury outcomes, and to examine training dose and adherence as potential effect modifiers. Methods Randomised controlled trials evaluating exercise-based IPPs in female team-sport athletes were synthesised. Risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using random-effects models. Subgroup analyses examined training frequency, session duration, weekly training dose, and adherence, while meta-regression was used to examine study-level associations with training dose and adherence. Results Thirteen unique trials involving 13,675 athletes were included. IPPs reduced overall injury risk by 35% (RR = 0.65, 95% CI: 0.53–0.79), with a similar reduction in lower-limb injuries (RR = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.53–0.86). Significant reductions were also observed for anterior cruciate ligament injuries (RR = 0.62, 95% CI: 0.43–0.89) and ankle injuries (RR = 0.59, 95% CI: 0.42–0.84). Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested larger effects at 4–5 sessions/week (RR = 0.47) and 21–30 min/session (RR = 0.42). Programmes providing 51–120 min/week were associated with greater risk reduction than those providing 1–50 min/week (RR = 0.48 vs. 0.80). title: Blood-Brain Barrier Development and Treatment Response in Pediatric Brain Tumors: A Review
abstract: Pediatric brain tumors remain a leading cause of cancer-related mortality in children, partially due to ineffective delivery of systemic therapies across the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Unlike adults, the pediatric blood–brain barrier (BBB) in infants undergoes significant postnatal maturation during the first year of life, resulting in age-dependent differences in permeability, transporter expression, and barrier regulation. The project examines how BBB immaturity and blood-brain tumor barrier (BBTB) heterogeneity influence the delivery discrepancy, efficacy and toxicity of antitumor drugs (chemotherapy, targeted therapies, and radiation), and the development of emerging, novel antitumor drug delivery tools for infantile brain tumors. This review distinguishes between the developing physiological BBB and the pathological BBTB, which may exhibit regionally increased or decreased permeability depending on tumor biology. Through a structured review of current literature, the study aims to identify why therapeutic strategies for adult brain tumor patients fail to translate to pediatric brain tumor populations and highlight clinical implications of the BBB in drug resistance, toxicity, and therapeutic design.

Relaxation in action: enhanced vagal modulation during Virabhadrasana (a standing yoga-asana) despite orthostatic demand suggests efficient regulation of effort
abstract: Introduction Classical Yoga-Āsana emphasizes not merely adoption of posture, but progressive reduction of unnecessary effort while maintaining stable engagement. However, the neurophysiological implications of effort modulation during yoga practice remain insufficiently understood. This study examined whether externally similar Yoga-Āsana performed with different effort organization may engage distinct autonomic regulatory organizations. Methods Eight experienced female yoga practitioner-teachers (median age: 58 years; median yoga experience: 19 years) participated in a within-subject exploratory study. Heart rate variability (HRV) was assessed during three 5-min conditions: free-standing, effort-reduced “yogic” Virabhadrasana (Y), and Virabhadrasana (E) performed without deliberate effort reduction. HRV indices were analysed using Friedman and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm–Bonferroni correction. Results Compared with Virabhadrasana (E), yogic Virabhadrasana (Y) demonstrated significantly increased RR interval, HF power and HF (nu), and significantly reduced LF (nu) and LF/HF ratio indicating preserved vagally mediated autonomic flexibility despite similar orthostatic demand and active postural engagement. DFAα1 values were significantly lower in the yogic condition. Discussion This study provides preliminary proof-of-concept that externally similar but effortfully diffe…

title: أنماط الاستجابة في الدعوة إلى الله تعالى (دراسة وصفية استقرائية)
abstract: تناول البحث أنماط الاستجابة في الدعوة إلى الله تعالى، وهدف إلى التعرف على أنماط الاستجابة في الدعوة إلى الله ومصادرها، وبيان العوامل المؤثرة في أنماط استجابة المدعوين، وتوضيح أساليب التعامل مع أنماط الاستجابة. وقد استخدمت الباحثة لتحقيق هذه الأهداف المنهج الاستقرائي، والمنهج الوصفي. وتم التوصل إلى عدد من النتائج، أبرزها: تتعدد أنماط استجابة المدعوين للدعوة الإسلامية بين القبول، والتردد، والرفض، ويعود هذا التفاوت إلى اختلاف العوامل المؤثرة في الاستجابة، مما يدل على أن التفاعل مع الدعوة ظاهرة مركبة تتداخل فيها أبعاد نفسية واجتماعية وثقافية متعددة. كما تتأثر الاستجابة الإيجابية للدعوة بعوامل ذاتية تتصل باستعداد المدعو ووعيه وسلامة فطرته، إلى جانب عوامل خارجية تتمثل في البيئة الاجتماعية والثقافية المحيطة به، حيث يسهم هذا التفاعل في تشكيل مواقفه وردود أفعاله تجاه الخطاب الدعوي. وتؤدي البيئة الاجتماعية والمجتمع المحيط دورًا مؤثرًا في توجيه أنماط الاستجابة، إذ قد تكون عامل دعمٍ للقبول والانفتاح، أو سببًا في التردد والرفض، تبعًا لطبيعة القيم السائدة والضغوط الاجتماعية. ومما أوصت به الباحثة: تعزيز الوعي المنهجي لدى الدعاة بأهمية فهم تنوّع أنماط استجابة المدعوين، وربط الخطاب الدعوي بالسياقات النفسية والاجتماعية والثقافية المحيطة، بما يمكّن من تقديم دعوة أكثر واقعية وحكمة وفاعلية.

title: Risk-Adjusted Performance of ESG ETFs: Benchmark, Geographic, and Market Exposure Analysis
abstract: This paper examines whether the risk-adjusted performance of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG)-focused Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) reflects distinct investment behavior or is primarily influenced by benchmark exposure, geography, and sector composition. Six ETFs are analyzed, including two ESG-based ETFs (ESGU and ESGD), two broad market benchmarks (SPY and VEA), a growth/technology ETF (QQQ), and a non-ESG ETF (VICEX). From accessible monthly closing price data for each ETF from December 2016 to May 2026, mean return, volatility, and Sharpe ratio values were calculated for each ETF over the whole period and across multiple distinct market sub-periods. Examining multiple market periods allows for comparison across varying economic and market conditions. This paper finds that ESG-focused ETFs do not clearly deliver consistently distinct or superior risk-adjusted performance. Instead, their returns appear largely explained by benchmark exposure, geography, and sector composition. Investors choosing ESG-based ETFs should not expect distinct, superior performance solely from ESG screening, as performance is largely based on other factors affecting the fund’s actual holdings.

title: Two-stage stochastic optimization for distribution networks considering demand response uncertainties
abstract: High penetration of distributed energy resources and uncertain loads creates financial and operational challenges for distribution networks. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a risk-averse, two-stage stochastic coordination framework for a distribution network interacting with the main grid. The day-ahead stage determines the procurement schedule, whereas the real-time stage corrects deviations through real-time market transactions and demand response (DR) mobilization. DR availability is explicitly modeled as scenario-dependent uncertainty. The physical network is formulated using a second-order cone programming (SOCP)-relaxed branch-flow model, which enables an exact mathematical decomposition of distribution locational marginal prices (DLMPs). A Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) metric is integrated to manage extreme tail-risk penalties. Simulations on the IEEE 33-bus system show that the proposed framework reduces the expected daily power shortage by over 10% compared with the risk-neutral baseline. Stronger risk aversion leads to more conservative day-ahead procurement. This forward over-procurement reduces expected real-time marginal scarcity, decreases the expected reliance on local DR during most hours, and dampens absolute DLMP levels at high-priced downstream nodes over a large portion of the operating horizon. title: Dual effects of anti-Müllerian hormone on ovarian response and fertilization in assisted reproductive technology cycles: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Objective To investigate the dual effects of anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) on ovarian response, fertilization outcomes, and clinical pregnancy in assisted reproductive technology (ART) cycles.Methods This retrospective cohort study screened 6,312 in vitro fertilization or intracytoplasmic sperm injection cycles performed between 2018 and 2023. After excluding cycles with missing AMH or body mass index (BMI) values, non-ART cycles, and extreme BMI values (<18 or ≥45 kg/m2), 4,399 cycles were included. AMH level, age, and BMI were evaluated as independent variables. Ovarian response (retrieved oocyte count) and normally fertilized embryos (two pronuclei) were analyzed using multivariable linear regression and clinical pregnancy was evaluated using logistic regression.Results AMH level showed a strong positive association with ovarian response (β=2.348; P<0.001), whereas age showed a significant negative association. After adjusting for age, BMI, fertilization method, and retrieved oocytes, AMH level showed a small but significant negative association with fertilized embryo count (β=-0.044; P=0.027). In the subgroup analysis, cycles with AMH ≥10 ng/mL showed higher oocyte yield but lower fertilization (0.561 vs. 0.694; P<0.001) and clinical pregnancy rates (5.7% vs. 23.10%; P<0.001) than those with AMH <10 ng/mL. title: Back to the future of sustainability: how social media influencers activate norms for sustainable fashion consumption among Gen Z
abstract: Purpose This study examines the impact of influencer marketing on Generation Z’s sustainable fashion consumption intention (SFCI) in Egypt by integrating the stimulus–organism–response (SOR) framework with the norm activation model (NAM). Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 268 Gen Z consumers in Egypt using a structured questionnaire. Structural equation modeling was used to test the research model, while multigroup analysis (MGA) using SmartPLS 4 was applied to test gender differences. Findings Influencer marketing significantly impacts two key norm-activation factors – awareness of consequences and personal norms, but not the ascription of responsibility, and these in turn predict Gen Z’s SFCI. The NAM variables partially mediate the relationship between influencer marketing and SFCI. MGA results reveal that the overall model is consistent across genders but uncover significant differences in specific psychological pathways. Practical implications The findings confirm the pivotal role of sustainability-focused fashion SMIs as actors and co-creators within the sustainable fashion ecosystem. By promoting recycled, upcycled, durable and economic fashion, their content can bridge the sustainability-positioned brands–consumer gap, activate personal norms and strengthen SFCI among Gen Z. title: Digital Financial Inclusion and Corporate Financing Constraints: Theoretical Mechanisms and Empirical Evidence from China
abstract: Using Chinese listed-firm data, this paper evaluates whether the development of digital inclusive finance at the city level is related to firms' external financing pressure and whether the external information environment offers a plausible explanation. The Digital Financial Inclusion Index for prefecture-level cities is linked to non-financial A-share firm observations over 2011-2023. The dependent variable is the logarithm of financing cost, and the regressions account for firm characteristics, industry effects, year effects, and within-firm correlation in the errors. The estimated coefficient on the digital-finance index is -0.0743 (p < 0.05), implying lower financing-cost pressure in cities with more developed digital inclusive finance. Digital finance is also positively related to analyst following and the number of research reports, which is consistent with wider production and circulation of firm-specific information. The negative coefficient is statistically significant in the non-state-owned and larger-firm subsamples, but not in the state-owned and smaller-firm subsamples; these subgroup regressions do not by themselves establish statistically significant cross-group differences. Lagging the digital-finance measure, changing the financing-cost definition, and introducing province effects do not overturn the main result. The evidence indicates that digital finance can …

title: Not My Fault: Exploring Neutralization Strategies Behind Employee Misconduct
abstract: This study examines the rationalization techniques employed by employees to justify workplace misconduct, revealing significant insights into their psychological processes. The findings indicate that Denial of Responsibility and Denial of Injury are the most commonly used strategies, allowing employees to distance themselves from their actions by attributing blame to external factors or minimizing the impact of their behavior. Additionally, moderate utilization of Denial of Victim and Appeal to Higher Authority suggests that some employees engage in a complex rationalization process, shifting blame onto others or framing their actions as serving a greater purpose. The reported misconduct behaviors—ranging from dishonesty to aggression—are accompanied by emotional responses like guilt and entitlement, reinforcing the use of rationalization to maintain a favorable self-image. Notably, the absence of techniques such as Condemnation of the Condemner indicates that certain rationalizations may be influenced by organizational culture. These findings highlight the interplay between individual choices, corporate environments, and cultural contexts in workplace deviance. By understanding these mechanisms, organizations can develop more effective interventions and foster a culture that promotes ethical behavior and accountability.
venue: International Journal of Business and Management

title: Non-predictive strategies for political risk management in international markets
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how Global South firms mitigate political risk when operating in armed conflict zones and politically unstable international markets. It addresses the limited understanding of how firms develop, mobilize and transfer institutional capabilities in highly unstable contexts, where traditional predictive approaches lose effectiveness. Specifically, it investigates how Brazilian firms mobilize immediate resources, relational networks and trust to transform uncertainty into opportunity, uncovering patterns of resilience, adaptability and organizational learning underexplored in the literature on the internationalization of Global South multinational enterprises. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a qualitative, multiple-case design grounded in an inductive approach, examining six Brazilian firms with operations in, or exposure to, conflict-affected or politically unstable environments. Primary data comprised seven semistructured interviews conducted between February and March 2023, complemented by documentary evidence including corporate documents, media coverage, export data and institutional reports. Data were analyzed through iterative open coding, second-order theming and cross-case pattern matching, with documentary triangulation enhancing construct validity. title: Workplace adoption of wearable devices: insights into Greek employees’ intentions and usage trends
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the factors influencing Greek employees’ intention to adopt wearable devices in the workplace, focusing on privacy management and trust. It addresses the organizational challenges of balancing innovation with employee concerns about surveillance and data protection. Design/methodology/approach Based on Privacy Calculus Theory, extended with trust, a research model was tested through a large-scale survey of 2,243 employees in Greece using structural equation modeling. Findings Perceived effectiveness of privacy policies, control and benefits strongly predicted adoption intention, while privacy concerns and risks acted as barriers. Trust showed limited direct effects, with its influence primarily operating through indirect relationships. The model explained 46% of adoption intention variance. Practical implications The findings highlight the importance for managers to design transparent privacy policies, strengthen employee control over data and build organizational trust to facilitate wearable integration into HR and productivity practices. Originality/value The study extends Privacy Calculus Theory to organizations, introduces institutional variables such as privacy policy effectiveness and clarifies trust’s indirect role. It provides new insights from a regional context rarely examined.
venue: Journal of Science and Technology Policy Management

Mimicking Leaves Asymmetric Multilayer Films for Reflection-Suppressed Electromagnetic Interference Shielding and Thermal Management
abstract: Abstract Developing electromagnetic interference shielding materials that synergize high shielding effectiveness with reflection-suppressed characteristics is critical for mitigating secondary radiation pollution, yet it remains a significant challenge. Inspired by the functional zonation of plant leaves, we herein design a multifunctional composite film with an asymmetric electric−magnetic multilayered structure via a layer-by-layer assembly strategy. Supported by a bacterial cellulose scaffold, the biomimetic film features a three-layer functional architecture: the top layer mimics the light-transmitting epidermis to facilitate impedance matching by introducing magnetic carbon-encapsulated cobalt hollow nanospheres (C─Co); the middle layer parallels the light-absorbing palisade tissue for efficient wave dissipation by synergizing liquid metal (LM) and C─Co; and the bottom layer serves as a robust reflection barrier using LM and Ti3C2Tx MXene, mimicking the internal light-trapping mechanism of leaves to reflect and reabsorb residual waves. Consequently, the composite film achieves a superior shielding effectiveness of 63.65 dB and a reflection effectiveness as low as 8.05 dB, effectively reconciling the intrinsic conflict between shielding and reflection in highly conductive materials. Simultaneously, the combination of outstanding mechanical flexibility and dual-mode thermal …

title: Why Port Automation Generates Conflict in Some Economies but Stability in Others: A Comparative Institutional Perspective Between China and the US
abstract: Over* 80% of global commodity trade relies on seaborne transportation, with container ports serving as pivotal hubs connecting upstream and downstream supply chain segments. Driven by surging maritime shipping demand and the pursuit of operational efficiency, intelligent port automation has evolved into an irreversible global trend. Though both China and the United States have promoted port digital upgrading, they adopt divergent reform paths, confront unique institutional dilemmas, and generate vastly different practical outcomes. This essay conducts a comparative case study focusing on Shanghai Yangshan Port and Los Angeles Port. It contrasts the implementation effects of automated transformation and corresponding labor relations systems in the two economies, and further explores the institutional, cultural and regulatory roots behind their performance gaps. The analysis reveals that the Chinese port operation framework achieves prominent advantages in handling efficiency and supply chain stability, while its hidden drawbacks in worker welfare and employment equity are also discussed to deliver balanced conclusions and targeted policy suggestions.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Explainable Machine Learning for Home Equity Line of Credit Risk Assessment: A Multi-Model Comparison with SHAP Interpretability
abstract: Accurate default risk prediction is essential for commercial banks' retail credit loan decisions and supervision. Traditional credit scoring models fail to provide clear decision schemes under strict regulation, while high-performance machine learning models face the black-box dilemma, making it difficult to meet financial regulatory requirements for model transparency. Based on the HELOC benchmark data released by FICO, this study investigates machine learning applications in credit risk prediction and benchmarks six models: random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, logistic regression, and SVM. Of the six models evaluated, CatBoost recorded the highest AUC at 0.7923; robustness assessments, however, showed that the margins separating the models fell short of statistical significance. We then applied SHAP to interrogate the basis of these predictions. Three features emerged as the dominant drivers of HELOC risk: external risk estimation, revolving credit burden, and the average length of credit history. For credit risk practitioners, these variables deserve the closest attention when reviewing HELOC applications. More broadly, the findings indicate that interpretable machine learning can give lenders a defensible account of every credit decision — a capability that serves both regulatory oversight and the individuals whose applications are under review.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Multiplexed catheter-integrated pressure sensing system for endoluminal interventions
abstract: Abstract Advances in flexible catheters pave the way for minimally invasive diagnosis and treatment of luminal organs and tubular structures through endoluminal interventions. A key challenge is in establishing non-constraining pressure monitoring at the interfaces between medical catheters and intraluminal anatomy, where catheter–tissue interactions may be influenced by lumen curvature, structural variability, and physiological motion. In this work, we present a scalable and multi-purpose pressure sensing system for multidirectional monitoring of tissue interactions, establishing a robust solution for deploying diagnostic and therapeutic instruments in various types of endoluminal interventions. This approach provides an integrated pressure sensing platform that combines a thin-film piezoelectric sensor array with a bespoke multi-lumen catheter and a custom signal acquisition circuit. The sensor array is fabricated from an ultrathin poly (vinylidene fluoride-co-trifluoroethylene) (P(VDF-TrFE)) film using a multilayer sandwich architecture with patterned gold electrodes, resulting in a flexible device with a total thickness of approximately 20 µm and sensing units as small as 2.25 mm 2 . The multi-lumen catheter is fabricated with a cost-effective and highly scalable fiber drawing technology, establishing a means of fast prototyping catheters with bespoke microstructures for se…

title: Analysis of the Impact of L'Oréal's Scarcity Marketing on Brand Premium Capability
abstract: Some high-end cosmetic brands have begun to use scarcity marketing in recent times to create a sense of urgency for consumers and boost the demand for their products. L'Oréal Paris is a well-known mass-market beauty brand, and this paper will investigate how scarcity marketing devices, such as holiday-limited gift sets, joint-brand drop collaborations, and time-limited flash sales, affect its brand premium capacity. Time-limited and quantity-restricted offers can increase the demand for purchase by creating a sense of urgency (FOMO) and making the limited items more desirable social status symbols in the short run. However, this study has also shown some serious long-term problems: frequent alterations in the surface packaging, a deviation from L'Oréal's core scientific identity, and controversial "faux-scarcity" behaviour will inevitably lead to scarcity fatigue and a loss of consumer trust. To address the above problems and avoid the controversy of an "IQ tax", this paper proposes some feasible optimisation directions: align scarcity campaigns with the company's core values, innovate experiential scarcity through digital integration, and build a transparent tiered pricing system. In short, the above measures can help beauty brands continuously use the concept of scarcity to build brand value without damaging the brand image.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: The light side of mast cell degranulation: delivering macrophage repair through molecular condensates
abstract: Abstract Mast cell (MC) degranulation is commonly viewed as the rapid release of preformed inflammatory mediators into the extracellular environment. In a recent study published in the Journal of Experimental Medicine, Salm et al. described a more spatially controlled form of MC communication following sterile peritoneal injury. Sensory neurons activated MCs through substance P signaling, promoting the release of extracellular granules that persisted as membraneless biomolecular condensates. These condensates, enriched in more than 200 proteins, remained associated with the surface of large peritoneal macrophages (LPMs), where they contributed to rapid macrophage aggregation through the scavenger receptor MARCO and promoted a repair-like phenotype at the injury site. Lattice light sheet microscopy further revealed F-actin-containing cytonemes that captured condensates from the MC surface and distributed them to surrounding macrophages. Importantly, disruption of this process impaired condensate dispersion, LPM recruitment, and wound healing. The study expands the conventional view of MC degranulation beyond the release of inflammatory soluble mediators by showing that released granules can remain organized and be actively positioned within injured tissue, creating a localized communication system between sensory neurons, MCs, and macrophages.

title: The Impact of Supply Chain Resilience on Corporate Green Innovation: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Listed Firms
abstract: Against a backdrop of frequent external shocks and an accelerating green transition, this study examines whether supply chain resilience improves firms' current green innovation. Using 2004-2024 panel data for Chinese A-share listed firms, we construct supply chain resilience as the sum of entropy-weighted resistance and recovery indices. Two-way fixed-effects estimates show that all three measures significantly increase green patent applications. The findings remain robust to leave-one-out industry-year instrumental-variable estimation, alternative samples, expanded controls, and an alternative resilience measure. Mechanism tests indicate that resilience supports green R&D by easing financing constraints and reducing agency costs, while corporate reputation and ownership concentration improve the conversion of resilience resources into innovation. The effect differs across listing boards, ownership types, and factor intensities: it is stronger for non-GEM, state-owned, and labor-intensive firms, but becomes negative for GEM firms. Supply chain resilience is therefore not merely an operational safeguard; it is also an organizational capability that sustains green innovation. The evidence provides a firm-level basis for jointly advancing supply chain security and green transformation.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Management of bone cement leakage after percutaneous vertebroplasty in a geriatric patient with multimorbidity: a case report
abstract: Rationale Although percutaneous vertebroplasty (PVP) is a minimally invasive treatment for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures, bone cement leakage remains a serious complication. Management becomes particularly challenging in elderly patients with multiple comorbidities. Patient concerns An 84-year-old woman with severe osteoporosis underwent PVP for a T10 vertebral fracture. Postoperatively, she developed progressive low back pain, bilateral lower limb weakness, and urinary dysfunction. She had multiple comorbidities, including pulmonary embolism, coronary artery disease, grade 3 hypertension, and deep vein thrombosis, which significantly increased perioperative risk. Diagnoses Primary diagnosis: Intraspinal space-occupying lesion secondary to bone cement leakage after PVP, with thoracic spinal cord injury and incomplete paraplegia. Direct complication: Intraspinal cement leakage at T10 with spinal cord compression. Relevant comorbidities included pulmonary embolism, postherpetic neuralgia, pulmonary hypertension, lumbar stenosis, and multiple systemic conditions. Interventions After multidisciplinary team consultation, the patient underwent posterior thoracic laminectomy, removal of leaked cement, pedicle screw fixation with bone cement augmentation at adjacent levels, and bone grafting. Perioperative management included anticoagulation adjustment, electrolyte corre…

title: Temporal changes in auditory adverse event reporting in the U.S. vaccine adverse event reporting system associated with the COVID-19 vaccine rollout: an interrupted time series analysis with negative control evaluation
abstract: Objectives To assess whether auditory adverse event (AE) reporting changed after the COVID-19 vaccine rollout, and whether any change reflected a true safety signal or a shift in reporting behavior. Methods We analyzed U.S. Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) data from 2018 through 2025 using interrupted time series (ITS) analysis. The COVID-19 vaccine Emergency Use Authorization (EUA), granted in the fourth quarter of 2020, was treated as a time-level ecological intervention. Because VAERS receives reports for all vaccines, we included every report regardless of vaccine type. We then modeled quarterly auditory AE reporting rates before and after the EUA. Sensitivity analyses stratified results by age, fit quasi-Poisson regression models, used dermatologic events as a reporting-propensity sentinel serving much like a negative control, and compared auditory AE proportions across vaccine types after the EUA (COVID-19 versus influenza versus other). Results Of 1,347,820 reports, 27,750 involved auditory AEs. Reporting rates rose immediately after the EUA ( β = 2,317.4, 95% CI 1,079.1–3,555.6; p < 0.001). Count-based models incorporating an offset for total reporting confirmed this finding: quasi-Poisson yielded an IRR of 7.14 (95% CI 1.63–31.33; p = 0.015), negative binomial an IRR of 5.62 (95% CI 3.29–9.62; p < 0.001), and quasi-binomial an OR of 7.36 (95% CI 1.6…

title: A Study on the Impact of Technological Efficiency and Financial Sustainability on the Sustainable Development Pathways of Chinese Commercial Banks un der Asymmetric Fintech Shocks
abstract: Fintech creates significant asymmetric shocks within the banking sector. These shocks have a deep influence on the sustainable development of commercial banks. This study uses balanced panel data from 42 Chinese commercial banks, covering the period from 2019 to 2024. It builds an analytical framework called "Fintech Asymmetric Shocks—Technological Efficiency—Bank Sustainability." Empirical tests are then carried out. These tests rely on the entropy iight method, the DEA-Malmquist model, and a moderated mediation model. The results show that the impact of fintech asymmetric shocks on sustainable development varies greatly among different types of Chinese commercial banks. Technical efficiency plays a partial mediating role in this process. Patent reserves, listing status, and asset size all have positive moderating effects. Moreover, when patent reserves reach a certain level, the moderating effect becomes noticeably stronger. Looking across different bank types, large state-owned commercial banks benefit positively. Joint-stock commercial banks experience a iak positive effect. In contrast, city commercial banks and rural commercial banks face major constraints. Therefore, this paper proposes different sustainability pathways and suggests category-based regulations tailored to each type of commercial bank.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Optimization and Collaborative Development of Enterprise Logistics under the Background of Digital Supply Chain
abstract: The application of big data, Internet of Things (IoT), and blockchain technologies has reshaped the operational logic of modern supply chains. Conventional logistics models, characterized by fragmented information flows, divergent decision-making objectives across supply chain participants, and suboptimal resource utilization, struggle to cope with volatile market demands and the coordination requirements of multi-stakeholder systems. Through a systematic literature review and comparative case analysis of representative enterprises, this study investigates the mechanisms by which digital supply chains enhance logistics performance. It identifies key barriers to cross-organizational logistics collaboration and proposes improvement measures across technological, organizational, and cooperative dimensions. Findings indicate that standardized digital information-sharing platforms can reduce average inventory turnover cycles by 12% to 18%, while stable collaborative governance mechanisms effectively lower overall logistics costs across the industrial chain. The analysis reveals that the primary obstacles to logistics collaboration include heterogeneous system interfaces, insufficient trust mechanisms for data sharing, and misaligned benefit distribution rules. The optimization strategies outlined in this paper offer practical guidance for manufacturing and retail firms undergoing di…
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: The Impact of Senior Executives' Perceptions of Sustainability on the Level of Green Technological Innovation in Enterprises
abstract: Regarding the background of "dual carbon" and high-quality development, it is a hot topic for both academics and industries about corporate green transformation. Based on hierarchical theory, this paper selects Chinese A-share listed companies from 2014-2024 as its research sample, empirically examines the effect of senior executives' green awareness on firms' level of green technological innovation, and further explores the mediating role of ESG performance. The findings show that: (1) senior executives' green awareness exerts a significant positive driving effect on a firm's level of green technological innovation, and this dominant influence remains robust under stability tests conducted with a shorter sample interval. (2) The results of the mediation analysis indicate that ESG performance acts as a crucial 'bridge' between executives' green awareness and the level of corporate green technological innovation; that is, executives' green awareness significantly enhances the firm's substantive green innovation output by optimising its overall performance across environmental, social and governance dimensions. (3) Heterogeneity analysis reveals that polluting firms are more sensitive and responsive to incentives for green innovation than non-polluting firms.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Assessment of residual Salmonella contamination in German broiler farms and their surroundings after cleaning and disinfection
abstract: Abstract The presence of Salmonella on broiler farms after cleaning and disinfection (C&D) poses a significant risk to public health as Salmonella remains a leading cause of human foodborne infections. In this study, retrospective investigations were conducted to evaluate the persistence of non-typhoidal Salmonella after C&D. Samples were collected from 21 German broiler farms which had a recent history of Salmonella contamination. Samples were collected after the C&D process over a period of seven years. A total of 1,200 swab samples from different locations inside and outside the poultry houses were tested for the presence of Salmonella using real-time polymerase chain reaction, followed by culture confirmation and biochemical serovar identification of positive samples. Sampling locations were classified into four Risk Groups based on their spatial proximity to the broilers and the associated likelihood of direct or indirect Salmonella transmission. Salmonella was detected in 27.6% of swab samples ( n = 331), with S. Infantis ( n = 162; 48.9%) and S. Java ( n = 52; 15.7%) being the predominant serovars. A significant difference was observed between positive internal samples (25.1%) and positive external samples (34.5%). The highest percentage of positive samples was found in Risk Group 4, which involved areas outside of farm buildings with minimal human contact. Additionally,…

Mandate-Based Evaluation of Médecins Sans Frontières’ Crisis Management in the Gaza Strip: A Mixed-Methods Study with Comparative Insights from Lebanon and Syria
abstract: Despite extensive humanitarian operations in conflict zones, limited empirical and mandate-based evaluations have examined Médecins Sans Frontières’ (MSF) crisis management performance in the Gaza Strip using field-based data. This study evaluates MSF’s effectiveness in crisis management in Gaza in light of its humanitarian mandate and provides comparative insights from Lebanon and Syria. A mixed-method design was employed, combining a structured survey administered to 43 emergency healthcare staff at Shuhada Al-Aqsa Hospital with qualitative interviews involving local stakeholders. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and one-way ANOVA. Findings revealed a strong positive correlation between the adequacy of training resources and staff qualification (r = 0.72, p < 0.01). ANOVA results showed significant differences in the application of learned skills across professional categories (F = 4.86, p = 0.03), with nurses reporting greater operational difficulties than physicians. While training programs were highly rated (M = 4.72), logistical barriers, time constraints, and security instability limited the practical implementation of acquired competencies. Comparative observations suggest that MSF’s operations in Gaza face greater structural and geopolitical constraints than in Lebanon. The study contributes a field-informed, mandate-ba…

title: Managing sustainability under uncertainty: how executive paradoxical cognition shapes dynamic capabilities and ESG outcomes
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how sustainability initiatives are shaped under conditions of regulatory ambiguity and market turbulence, focusing on how executive paradoxical cognition influences the activation of dynamic capabilities and the translation of internal adaptation into externally recognized environmental, social and governance (ESG) legitimacy. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a sequential mixed-methods design combining a sector-wide survey of banking institutions with in-depth qualitative interviews across diverse ownership forms. Structural relationships are examined using partial least squares structural equation modelling, while qualitative pattern matching is used to interpret the cognitive and organizational processes underlying the observed relationships. Findings The results of this study show that environmental uncertainty strengthens paradoxical cognition, which in turn supports the activation of dynamic capabilities related to sensing, seizing and reconfiguring. Capability development alone, however, does not translate directly into enhanced ESG legitimacy. When paradoxical cognition is more pronounced, internal adaptation becomes harder to stabilize as external legitimacy, as ongoing experimentation and reconfiguration increase interpretive complexity and stakeholder scrutiny. Qualitative evidence further indicates that while paradoxica…

title: Beyond content knowledge: fostering pre-service social studies teachers' social and emotional competencies
abstract: Purpose Increased classroom volatility, uncertainty, complexity and ambiguity (Hadar et al., 2020; Pace and Stoddard, 2025) has heightened the need for social studies educators to be competent in the soft skills integral to navigating controversy and civic preparation, operationalized here as social and emotional competencies (SEC). Seizing opportunity in challenge, our team of university instructor-researchers piloted a Lesson Study Lab (LSL), which promoted pre-service social studies teachers' competencies in collaborative C3 inquiry planning and instruction (Weaver et al. 2025). The current study explored the question: Is the lesson study process associated with change in pre-service social studies teachers' SEC and teaching practices? Design/methodology/approach This article describes the LSL program, serving pre-service social studies teachers in our Midwestern state university, and the accompanying quantitative pretest-posttest quasi-experimental study of participants' social and emotional instruction and competencies. Findings Paired sample t-test analyses indicated that our (n = 69) pre-service teachers reported significant growth in social and emotional instructional interactions as well as social awareness, relationship skills, responsible decision-making and providing feedback after participating in the one-semester lab experience. Originality/value SEL researchers h…

title: Dynamic Identification of Hotel Service Experience Quality Based on Semantic Mining of Online Reviews
abstract: This study develops a dynamic framework for identifying hotel service experience quality through semantic mining of online reviews. Ctrip reviews from 260 hotels in Shanghai, Beijing, Guangzhou, Chengdu, and Hangzhou between 2021 and 2024 were cleaned into 156,000 valid reviews and 10,842 hotel-month observations. The framework combines a service-experience ontology, dependency-based aspect extraction, SKEP sentiment scoring, complaint intensity, change-point detection, and Gaussian hidden Markov modeling across eight service dimensions. Results show that semantic indicators detect deterioration earlier than numerical ratings, especially in cleanliness, facility reliability, and problem recovery, where complaint intensity rose 18%–27% above the sample mean during risk periods. The model classifies four quality states and achieves an F1-score of 0.829 and AUC of 0.903 for predicting next-month service decline, providing a reproducible method for dynamic hotel quality monitoring.

title: Increasing urogenital and oropharyngeal gonorrhoea positivity in women attending a sexual health service in Melbourne, Australia, 2015–2024
abstract: Background Gonorrhoea notifications among women have increased, but the determinants of this trend are unclear. We aimed to examine temporal trends in gonorrhoea positivity and associated clinical characteristics among women attending a major sexual health clinic in Melbourne, Australia between 2015 and 2024. Method We conducted a retrospective analysis of women diagnosed with gonorrhoea between 2015 and 2024. Demographic, behavioural and clinical data were extracted from routine clinical records, including sexual practices, sex work status and condom use. A chart review of a subset of positive cases was performed to obtain symptom characteristics and microscopy findings. Results Over the study period, we included a total of 91,332 consultations (47,013 women), with a gonorrhoea test performed on the day. Overall, the gonorrhoea positivity was 1.9% (1693/91,332), and it increased from 1.3% (61/4711) in 2015 to 2.3% (243/10,497) in 2024 (Ptrend < 0.001), representing a 78.9% relative increase. Oropharyngeal gonorrhoea increased from 4.4% (21/482) to 5.8% (96/1653; Ptrend < 0.001), and urogenital gonorrhoea increased from 1.0% (49/4673) to 1.7% (181/10,435; Ptrend < 0.001), whereas anorectal gonorrhoea remained stable. Of the 1693 women who were diagnosed with gonorrhoea, most were born overseas (52.9%, n = 896), and resided in high socioeconomic areas (76.1%, n = 1289).…

title: Delivering prehabilitation in cancer surgery: a service evaluation at Nottingham University Hospitals
abstract: Abstract Purpose To evaluate outcomes of a multimodal prehabilitation service for cancer surgery patients delivered through three pathways (Specialised, Targeted, Universal) within routine NHS care at Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust. Methods This was a retrospective observational service evaluation of routine care data collected between 2022 and 2025. Of 1961 referred patients, 1720 were analysed: Specialised ( n = 329), Targeted ( n = 943), and Universal ( n = 448). Multimodal prehabilitation included exercise, nutrition, and psychological support, stratified by risk. Functional capacity was assessed using the Incremental Shuttle Walk Test (ISWT), 60-s Sit-to-Stand (STS), and grip strength. Psychological well-being was measured using the Generalised Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). Physical activity behaviour was also recorded. Results All pathways showed significant within-group improvements. ISWT increased by 57 m ( p < 0.001, d = 0.6) and STS by 6 repetitions ( p < 0.001, d = 0.9). Anxiety (Δ –1.9) and depression (Δ –2.0) scores decreased (both p < 0.001, d ≈ –0.5). Weekly physical activity rose by 142 min ( d = 1.07), and strength sessions increased by 2.4 per week ( d = 1.1). Between-group differences were limited: PHQ-9 improved more in Specialised versus Targeted, and strength sessions increased more in Universal versus T…

title: Subscription Parking Usage Behavior in Medan: An Integrated Theory of Planned Behavior and Service Quality Model
abstract: Background: Subscription parking in Medan City aims to improve parking services, transparency, and local revenue. However, public participation remains low, indicating that policy success depends on user behavior. Previous studies have rarely integrated the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), service quality, and satisfaction to explain subscription parking usage in a public-sector context. Objective: This study aims to analyze public perceptions of subscription parking implementation, examine the factors influencing subscription parking usage behavior, and provide recommendations for improving policy implementation in Medan City. Methods: A quantitative survey was conducted among 390 subscription parking users in Medan City. Respondents were selected using purposive sampling based on their status as registered subscription parking users and their experience using the service. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). Results: Service quality was the strongest determinant of user satisfaction (β = 0.757; p < 0.001), while attitude was the strongest direct determinant of usage behavior (β = 0.748; p < 0.001). Service quality also influenced usage behavior through satisfaction and attitude, including a significant serial mediation effect (β = 0.258; p < 0.001). Subjective norms …
venue: Journal of Business, Social and Technology

title: Development of and satisfaction with a short-term outpatient preventive medical service for working informal caregivers: a study protocol of a non-randomized prospective pilot study
abstract: Abstract Background About 80% of care receivers (CRs) in Germany are cared for at home by family members or friends. These informal caregivers (CGs) often report a high burden from caregiving, which negatively affects their mental and physical health and often results in reduced work hours. CGs with statutory health insurance can apply for preventive medical services. A change in the law has allowed the duration of service to be split. Recent research postulated specialized digital and analog multi-component interventions to protect CGs’ health, which the pAKur project wants to develop and implement into public health. This pilot will focus on the development of and satisfaction with an outpatient preventive medical service for CGs. Methods The non-randomized, prospective pilot study will be performed on-site in Oberstdorf, Bavaria (Germany) and online from April 2026 to January 2027. Working CGs with a moderate CG burden caring for a CR with a moderate need for assistance will be included. The intervention will be developed in participation with CGs and experts in the corresponding field. Two groups (A and B) will participate in the same on-site treatment but will differ in the intensity of the digital support phase (A: low; B: high) and the location of the refresher treatment (A: on-site; B: digital). Within the framework of a mixed-methods design, quantitative and qualitativ…

title: Experiential over functional: how intrinsic motivation and identity drive virtual goods consumption in digital service platforms
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate why experiential value attributes systematically outweigh functional and social value dimensions in driving purchase intentions for character-based virtual goods in F2P digital platforms. Drawing on the theory of consumption value, self-determination theory, and extended self theory, the study develops an integrative framework explaining how motivational internalization and identity incorporation produce the observed dominance of experiential value. The study addresses a persistent theoretical gap in consumer value research by identifying the psychological mechanisms through which certain value dimensions translate into sustained behavioral commitment while others do not. Design/methodology/approach This study employs a theory-testing survey design administered to 192 active players of a character-centric free-to-play (F2P) platform. Respondents were recruited from an official online community dedicated to the focal game. All constructs were measured using multi-item scales adapted from established literature and assessed on seven-point Likert scales. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was used to test hypothesized relationships among consumption value dimensions, attitude, and purchase intention. Reliability and validity were confirmed via Cronbach's alpha, composite reliability, average variance extracted, and the Fornell–Larcker criteri…

title: Unleashing the power of a smile: the impact of customer humor on employees' proactive customer service performance
abstract: Purpose Drawing on social exchange theory, this study investigates whether and how customer humor affects employees' proactive customer service performance (PCSP). Specifically, we propose customer–employee exchange (CEX) as the mediating mechanism and employee extraversion as a boundary condition. Design/methodology/approach Hypotheses were examined using two independent studies. Study 1 employed an online scenario-based experiment (N = 146). Study 2 used a three-wave, multi-source survey of frontline hospitality employees in China (N = 340). Findings Results across the two studies show that customer humor is positively related to employees' PCSP. This relationship is consistent with an indirect effect through CEX, indicating that customer humor may contribute to higher-quality exchange relationships, which in turn are associated with employees' proactive service behaviors. In addition, higher extraversion strengthens the positive effect of customer humor on CEX and, consequently, reinforces the indirect effect of customer humor on PCSP through CEX. Originality/value This study advances humor research in hospitality by shifting attention from intra-organizational humor to customer-initiated humor as an external interpersonal cue that shapes employee behavior. By identifying CEX as a key mediating mechanism and extraversion as a boundary condition, the study clarifies when and …
venue: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics

title: AI transparency and bias mitigation in customer service: how ethical culture shapes customer trust
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine an unresolved issue in artificial intelligence (AI) driven customer service: Why transparency and bias mitigation do not automatically translate into customer trust across organizational contexts. Specifically, this study investigates the effects of bias mitigation strategies and AI transparency on customer trust, and the moderating role of organizational ethical culture, in the context of China. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey of 1,450 customers using generative AI services in banking and e-commerce was conducted. Adapted scales measured perceptions of AI transparency, bias mitigation, customer trust and organizational ethical culture. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling via a two-step approach: assessment of the measurement model (reliability and validity), followed by the structural model to test hypothesized relationships. Multiple regression served as a supplementary robustness check. Findings The study found that both bias mitigation strategies (β = 0.30, p < 0.001) and AI transparency (β = 0.35, p < 0.001) significantly enhance customer trust. Additionally, organizational ethical culture moderated these effects, amplifying them (β = 0.20 and 0.18, p < 0.01). These results emphasize the importance of transparency and fairness in AI, particularly in organizations with s…
venue: International Journal of Ethics and Systems

title: Electoral impact of the rental market: evidence from Israel
abstract: Abstract This paper studies housing tenure and voting patterns during the period from July 2013 to July 2023 in Israel, where the rental share of housing units increased from 24% to 29%, and six national elections for parliament took place. Using detailed neighbourhood panel data on rental units share and electoral outcomes, I find that switching a neighbourhood's housing stock from fully owner‐occupied into fully rental causes the turnout rate to decrease by 8–10 percentage points. These effects are interpreted with the aid of census and survey data, a fixed effects model and a control function approach. The findings contribute to understanding how housing market dynamics influence democracies.

title: From boundaryless work to labor-market adjustment: a multistage model of overtime pay insecurity, pay-related distress and mobility intentions
abstract: Purpose In digitally connected workplaces, overtime increasingly manifests as boundary penetration into nonwork time, complicating the recording, verification and remuneration of extra work. This study reframes overtime risk as a joint problem of boundary penetration and overtime-pay insecurity, examining a multistage pathway from overtime pay receipt status to pay-expectation-related work distress and, in turn, to multiple mobility intentions. Design/methodology/approach This study uses nationally representative microdata from Taiwan's Ministry of Labor 2025 Survey on the Living and Employment Situation of Labor to estimate a generalized structural equation model. The model examines the relationship between overtime pay receipt, distress and various mobility intentions, while controlling for worker, job, and institutional factors. Because the analysis is based on cross-sectional survey data, the estimated multistage pathway should be viewed as associative rather than strictly causal. While generalized structural equation modeling (GSEM) enables unified estimation of the multistage structure, this study does not provide bootstrapped confidence intervals for indirect effects. As a result, the mediation pattern should be considered suggestive rather than fully confirmed indirect-effect decomposition. Findings Overtime pay disadvantage reflects a governance failure in compensation…

title: Service Journey-Based Design for Sustainable Consumption Behavior Guidance and Feedback Reinforcement
abstract: The current study introduces a service journey-based design approach aimed at encouraging sustainable consumer choices in a digital environment of grocery shopping. A mobile shopping prototype named GreenCart Journey has been designed to provide pre-purchase guidance on sustainability, low-carbon purchase decision support, and post-checkout reinforcement feedback. The experiment took place during a four-week period among 120 university students including 60 people in the experimental group and 60 in the control group. The product database consisted of 180 grocery products distributed over six categories including information on price, packaging type, nutrition label, and carbon footprint. The research shows that by the end of Week 4 the ratio of low-carbon purchases of the experimental group is higher than that of the control group (0.64 ± 0.11 vs. 0.46 ± 0.13; p < .001). Furthermore, the average carbon score of the basket decreased by 18.72 ± 5.46 points, and sustainable substitution rate increased by 0.31 ± 0.08 (p < .001). These findings indicate that journey-based behavioral guidance and feedback reinforcement can transform sustainability information into repeated low-carbon purchase decisions.
