The market for ready-made clothing at the Zaporizhian Sich in the 18th century
abstract: Purpose. The purpose of this study is to reconstruct selected mechanisms underlying the functioning of the market for ready-made clothing, footwear, and accessories in the eighteenth-century Zaporizhian Sich. Methodology. The research is based on the principles of historicism, objectivity, and systematic analysis, employing comparative-historical, historical-typological, and source-critical methods. The scientific novelty. The study presents the comprehensive examination of the market for ready-made clothing, footwear, and accessories in the eighteenth-century Zaporizhian Sich as a distinct segment of its internal market. It systematically analyses the available source evidence concerning supply channels, product range, trade volume, market participants, forms of retailing, state regulation, and the pricing structure of this market segment. Conclusions. Ready-made clothing, footwear, and accessories constituted an important component of the eighteenth-century Zaporizhian Sich economy, representing not only elements of material culture but also an independent category of commodities operating within the internal market. The Zaporizhian region was supplied through several channels: the Hetmanate remained the principal source of mass-produced everyday goods, whereas the Crimean Khanate and the Ottoman Empire supplied expensive imported garments of Eastern origin. This supply struc…

title: Knowledge mobilization and work autonomy: from ambiguous directives to situated knowledge in public service delivery
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how public service employees resolve the tension between ambiguous directives and concrete work situations. It explores knowledge mobilization as a social process through which directives are transformed into situated knowledge for legitimate action, thereby enabling work autonomy. Design/methodology/approach The qualitative study was conducted in 2022 within Oslo municipality. Data were collected through observations and interviews across municipal schools and home care services. The analysis focuses on social interactions in physical and digital workplace spaces. Findings The findings reveal that knowledge mobilization occurs at the intersection of vertical dissemination and horizontal negotiation. These spaces include team meetings, open offices, informal clarification encounters and digital forums when discussion is enabled. Together, they enable the transformation of directives into situated knowledge and, consequently, support legitimate action. Originality/value This study contributes to workplace learning, knowledge management and policy implementation by identifying the central role of intersecting spaces for transforming directives into situated knowledge. It demonstrates that work autonomy, as a collectively legitimized capacity to act, is achieved through socially enabled knowledge mobilization within the frame of directives.

title: Strategic Positioning of Lightweight Soft Placement in AI-Animated Micro-Dramas: A Comparative Analysis of Brand Integration Models in China's Short-Form Video Market
abstract: With the rapid expansion of China's micro-drama market, brand integration has become a key marketing channel. This development has produced two distinct approaches to value creation: Hanshu's high-cost production and Proya's distributed placement. At the same time, generative AI tools such as ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 are reshaping marketing agencies' production capabilities. Thus, this study examines why lightweight soft placement creates value and how AI tools reshape marketing intermediaries' capabilities. Specifically, it uses a qualitative comparative case study based on industry reports from iResearch Center, Miaozhen Systems, and ThePaper, public campaign indicators, and Chinese industry media reports. On this basis, Hanshu and Proya are selected as comparative cases with similar market positioning but different brand integration strategies. The comparison indicates that lightweight placement is not a lower-value version of custom production. Its strength lies in risk distribution, iterative learning, and market reach. Moreover, the VRIO analysis shows that AI tool access alone provides limited advantage, while integrated workflows and client networks create more durable value.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: A Market-Aware Dynamic Trading Strategy Based on Unsupervised Clustering and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: The complexity and dynamics of the stock market make traditional absolute price prediction models based on supervised learning face great risks and limitations in practical business applications. This report proposes an innovative Hybrid Deep Reinforcement Learning trading framework to shift the forecast target from stock prices to optimal trading decisions in specific market conditions. The dataset for this experiment comes from a Malaysian listed company, GAMUDA BHD, from 2000 to 2024 on the Kaggle platform, and builds a decision-making structure with three stages. Use the Gaussian Mixture Model, the long-term and short-term memory network, and finally the Deep Q-Network to train the intelligent body to learn the optimal discrete trading strategy (buy, sell, hold) in a continuous complex environment. The research results show that, compared with the traditional buy-and-hold strategy and the single intensive learning model, the hybrid architecture that integrates market state perception shows significant commercial application value in terms of maximum pullback control and Sharp rate improvement. During a systemic market downturn, the GMM clusterer detected a surge in volatility, identifying the crisis. Based on this, DQN forced a "sell" order, successfully limiting the maximum drawdown. This strongly demonstrates the significance of hybrid models in mitigating black swan even…
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Ecosystem service valuation and management zoning of island evaluation units in the Miaodao Archipelago, Yellow-Bohai Sea
abstract: Introduction The 2024 adjustment of China’s marine ecological protection redlines increased the policy importance of small island systems and created a need for quantitative tools that link ecosystem service value (ESV) assessment with island-scale management zoning. This study evaluated 26 island evaluation units in the Miaodao Archipelago, a key area of Changdao National Park in the Yellow-Bohai Sea. Methods A modified equivalent factor method was used to monetize 11 ecosystem services at a 30 m grid scale. Island-specific adaptations included localizing the one-seventh rule, adjusting forest and grassland coefficients to reflect island productivity constraints, and setting food and raw-material services to zero where active farming was not represented in the land-cover data. Spatial sensitivity indicators were used as complementary references for zoning. Results The total ESV in 2020 was CNY 114.5468 million yr −1 , with a mean unit-area value of 20,194 CNY ha −1 yr −1 . Regulating and supporting services jointly accounted for 90.15% of the total. Discussion Coupling ESV with ecological sensitivity produced four management-oriented functional classes, providing quantitative support for Changdao National Park zoning and marine ecological redline implementation.

title: Building Tourist Loyalty in Cultural Museums: The Roles of Satisfaction, Destination Image, and Service Quality at Ullen Sentalu
abstract: Tourist loyalty is an important factor in sustaining the competitiveness and long-term attractiveness of cultural tourism destinations, particularly museums that rely on meaningful visitor experiences and positive perceptions. This study examines the effects of satisfaction, destination image, and service quality on tourist loyalty at the Ullen Sentalu Museum in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. A quantitative approach was employed using data collected from 110 tourists who had visited the museum. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares with SmartPLS version 3.29. The measurement model was evaluated through convergent validity, discriminant validity, composite reliability, and Cronbach’s alpha, while the structural model was assessed to examine the proposed relationships among the variables. The findings demonstrate that satisfaction, destination image, and service quality each have a positive and significant effect on tourist loyalty. Satisfaction shows the strongest influence, followed by destination image and service quality. The findings indicate that tourists who experience higher satisfaction, perceive a more favorable destination image, and receive better service are more likely to develop stronger loyalty toward the museum. These results highlight the importance of integrating visitor experience, destination positioning, and service delivery to strengthen tourist loyalty an…
venue: International Journal of Business, Economics, and Social Development

title: Supply Chain Finance Risks under Heterogeneous Market Structures: A Comparative Analysis of Monopoly, Oligopoly and Competitive Markets
abstract: Supply chain finance (SCF) has become an important financing mechanism for improving liquidity and supporting small and medium-sized enterprises. Existing research mainly focuses on credit risk, operational risk and digital financial technology, while paying limited attention to the role of market structure in shaping supply chain financial risks. This article explores how different market structures affect financing availability, liquidity pressure and risk transmission by comparing three representative industries - the power grid industry (monopoly), the electric vehicle industry (oligopoly) and the fast fashion industry (competitive market). The study draws on the theory of industrial organization, uses the Herfindahl - Hirschman Index (HHI) to assess market concentration, and employs the Cash Conversion Cycle (CCC) to evaluate working capital efficiency when comparable financial data is available. Research has found that monopolistic industries enjoy stable cash flows and lower financing risks, but they are still vulnerable to concentration risks. Oligopolistic industries demonstrate relatively efficient liquidity management and at the same time transfer financial pressure to suppliers through strong bargaining power. In contrast, suppliers in competitive markets face the greatest financing pressure due to weak bargaining power, long payment cycles and large fluctuations in…

title: An Evaluation Model for Community Social Service Responsiveness in Public Crises under Resilience Governance
abstract: In public crises, community social services are directly related to residents' demand response, vulnerable group protection, resource coordination, and post-crisis recovery. Conventional grassroots service evaluation often relies on post-event summaries and manual assessment. It is difficult to reveal differences among communities in response speed, demand matching, service equity, and recovery feedback in a timely manner. From the perspective of resilience governance, an evaluation model for community social service responsiveness is developed. Publicly available data from 2020 to 2024 are collected, including government service hotline monthly reports, community announcements, emergency management notices, civil affairs information, GDELT event records, and public Weibo texts. Public health emergencies, urban flooding, extreme weather, and temporary control events are transformed into computable community service event units. In terms of method, AHP and the entropy method are combined to generate composite weights and calculate responsiveness scores. An XGBoost regression model is then used for score prediction, while SHAP is applied to interpret key influencing factors. The results show that first response time, demand matching rate, cross-department coordination frequency, and vulnerable group coverage rate are the main variables affecting community service responsiveness. …

title: Determinants of Obesity among Market Women in the Kassena Nankana Municipality: A Cross-Sectional Analysis
abstract: This study examined the determinants of obesity among market women in the Kassena Nankana Municipality of Ghana, focusing on socio-demographic characteristics, dietary patterns, physical activity levels, and lifestyle behaviors. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 264 market women aged ≥18 years. Body Mass Index (BMI) and waist circumference (WC) were measured using standard protocols. Dietary intake was assessed using 24-hour dietary recalls and food frequency questionnaires. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was used to derive dietary patterns. Physical activity, meal skipping, work-related stress, and other lifestyle factors were evaluated using structured questionnaires. Chi-square tests, Fisher’s exact tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, and Kruskal-Wallis tests were used to examine associations between potential determinants and obesity status. Obesity prevalence was 54.2%, with 73.5% having abdominal obesity. Significant associations were found between obesity and age (p<0.001), with women aged 40-50 years showing the highest obesity rates (41.3%). Educational level was significantly associated with obesity (p=0.005), with 54.2% of women with no formal education being obese compared to 11.2% of those with tertiary education. Married women had significantly higher obesity rates (72.0%, p<0.001) than single women (7.7%). Type of housing showed a significant association w…
venue: American Journal of Food Science and Technology

title: Spreading word-of-mouth: the power of emotional satisfaction in dental clinics service narratives
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the influence of perceived service quality (PSQ) and service environment (SE) on key patient outcomes – clinic love (CL), clinic image (CI) and positive word-of-mouth (WOM) – within dental clinics, a utilitarian health-care context. It applies the stimulus–organism–response (S–O–R) framework to examine emotional dynamics within dental clinics, a utilitarian health-care context in a developing country. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative, cross-sectional survey was conducted with 211 patients at a leading dental clinic, using convenience sampling. Constructs were measured with validated multi-item scales, and hypotheses were tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to assess the hypothesized directional associations between service quality, SE, emotional satisfaction (ES) and outcomes (CL, CI and WOM). Findings The results demonstrate that PSQ and SE significantly enhance ES, which strongly drives CL, CI and positive WOM. In addition, both CL and CI directly foster WOM, highlighting their critical role in patient advocacy. These findings provide empirical support for the applicability of the S–O–R framework in utilitarian health-care contexts, emphasizing the pivotal influence of ES in shaping patient loyalty and clinic reputation. Originality/value This study contributes to the limited but growing re…
venue: International Journal of Pharmaceutical and Healthcare Marketing

title: The place and role of the “farewell sermon” in the regulation of interethnic relations in the Islamic world
abstract: This study addresses the reconstruction of the original religious and legal principles that facilitated the transformation of fragmented tribal society in seventh-century Arabia into a model of multi-ethnic integration. The relevance of the topic was determined by the need for reconstruction of original religious-legal norm to transform the Arab fragmentary tribalism into a model of multi-ethnic integration. The study aimed to determine what the normative core of the “Farewell Sermon” was and what role it played in the formation of mechanisms for supratribal social integration in the early Muslim community. The research was conducted through the contextual, comparative-historical, and textual analysis of three main source domains: homiletic (the “Farewell Sermon”), legal (the Constitution of Medina), and diplomatic (six letters of the Prophet), with a correlation with narrative and historiographic data on the social structure of early Islam. The results of the research revealed that in the Arabia of the 7th century there was a fragmented tribal, Jewish, and Christian society with no universal rules of interaction between groups. In this situation, the “Farewell Sermon” proclaimed several universal provisions: equality of people irrespective of their origin, individual responsibility instead of collective punishment, protection of vulnerable groups, rejection of ethnic superiori…

title: Differential regulation of SOCS signalling and immunoproteasome pathways by JAK inhibitors and TNF inhibitors in rheumatoid arthritis
abstract: Abstract Background Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors and TNF inhibitors (TNFi) are established therapies in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), yet their differential effects on the JAK/STAT/SOCS/proteasome axis remain incompletely understood. This pilot study systematically characterised treatment-specific effects of baricitinib, tofacitinib, and TNFi upon molecular signatures in RA patients. Methods Seventy-five patients with RA were enrolled across two prospective cohorts: an initial inception cohort treated with tofacitinib ( n = 15) and a subsequent confirmatory cohort treated with baricitinib or TNFi ( n = 60; baricitinib n = 29, TNFi n = 31), along with 17 and 33 healthy donors (HD)serving as controls for each cohort, respectively. mRNA expression of SOCS1, SOCS2, SOCS3, CIS1, and the immunoproteasome subunit β2i was assessed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells by real-time PCR. SOCS2 protein levels were measured by ELISA, and serum IL-6 levels were evaluated in the baricitinib/TNFi cohort. Results Responder rates were comparable across all three treatment groups at both time points. JAK inhibition was associated with a distinct SOCS suppression signature: SOCS2 mRNA declined progressively under both baricitinib and tofacitinib but not under TNFi blockade. SOCS1 and SOCS3 mRNA normalized under baricitinib over time, while SOCS3 elevation persisted throughout the observation period…

title: Weakly supervised machine learning for enhanced radio frequency interference detection in astronomical observations
abstract: Radio astronomical observations are prone to radio frequency interference (RFI) from manmade signals, including cellular transmissions, satellites, automotive radar, and others. Achieving harmonious spectrum sharing between the radio astronomy (RA) service and wireless systems requires identifying RFI in the vicinity of an RA telescope in real time. In this paper, we propose a weakly supervised generative adversarial network (GAN) for RFI detection in astronomical observations. Weakly supervised training is particularly effective when dealing with largely unlabeled datasets, as is the case with RA observations. At the same time, adversarial training through a GAN can enhance RFI detection under class imbalance. Our study is based on radio astronomical scans obtained from two telescopes: the 12-meter telescope at Kitt Peak, Arizona, operated by the Arizona Radio Observatory (ARO), and the Low-Frequency Array (LOFAR) telescope in the Netherlands. We further complemented these scans with a simulated dataset generated for the Hydrogen Epoch of Reionization Array (HERA) telescope. For the ARO dataset, the scans represent the measured temperature (equivalently, power density) of the telescope's antenna versus sky frequency over a 4 GHz bandwidth. We split each scan into 200 frequency channels (20 MHz per channel). A very small fraction of the dataset is manually labeled as clean or d…

title: Association between perceived school climate and employment anxiety among medical undergraduates: the mediating role of intentional self-regulation and the moderating role of perceived employability
abstract: Background Employment anxiety is an important psychological concern for medical undergraduates during the transition from university to work. This study examined the association between perceived school climate and employment anxiety and evaluated the roles of intentional self-regulation and perceived employability in this association. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 3,857 undergraduate students from four medical universities in Heilongjiang Province, China, between September and December 2025. Participants completed measures of perceived school climate, intentional self-regulation, perceived employability, employment anxiety, and demographic and academic characteristics. Hierarchical regression, indirect-association analysis, and moderated mediation analysis with 5,000 bootstrap resamples were performed. Multivariable models included university fixed effects and were adjusted for demographic and academic covariates. Results A more positive perceived school climate was associated with lower employment anxiety and stronger intentional self-regulation. Intentional self-regulation statistically accounted for part of the association between perceived school climate and employment anxiety. Perceived employability moderated the association between intentional self-regulation and employment anxiety: the negative association, and consequently the conditional indire…

title: Comparative evaluation of statistical and deep learning methods for high-frequency radar surface current forecasting in a narrow tropical strait
abstract: Accurate prediction of ocean surface currents is essential for maritime safety in narrow waterways with strong tidal forcing. This study presents a three-phase evaluation of forecasting methods for high-frequency (HF) radar surface currents in the Sunda Strait, Indonesia, where tidal currents regularly exceed 150 cm s −1 . Phase 1 compares twelve methods – persistence, tidal harmonics, classical time series, a reduced-rank spatio-temporal statistical model, shallow machine learning, and deep learning – for one-step-ahead prediction; evaluated consistently over all 291 grid cells and the full test period, the deep learning models achieve the lowest root-mean-square errors (RMSE) for both components, with the convolutional neural network (CNN) reaching 11.31 cm s −1 for the zonal component (skill score 0.50 relative to persistence) and the convolutional neural network–gated recurrent unit (CNN-GRU) reaching 15.44 cm s −1 for the meridional component (skill score 0.42); the pointwise classical statistical models (autoregressive integrated moving average, ARIMA; exponential smoothing) fall well below, while an empirical-orthogonal-function vector autoregression (EOF-VAR) that models spatial correlation closes most of the gap to deep learning, indicating that the neglect of spatial structure – not of nonlinearity – is the principal limitation of the classical baselines. Phase 2 exam…
venue: Advances in Statistical Climatology, Meteorology and Oceanography

title: Sensorimotor Alpha–Beta Phase–Amplitude Coupling Is Reduced in Adults Who Stutter and Predicts Stuttering Frequency: Implications for Gain Control
abstract: Abstract The sensorimotor dynamics that support speech motor stability remain incompletely understood. Developmental stuttering, which has been linked to dopaminergic dysregulation within basal ganglia–thalamo–cortical circuits, provides a useful model for probing these mechanisms. We tested whether alpha (α)–beta (β) phase–amplitude coupling (PAC) in sensorimotor mu rhythms is sensitive to sensorimotor regulatory processes, predicting that it would (a) differentiate adults who stutter (AWS) from fluent controls and (b) relate to the frequency of stuttered trials excluded from EEG analyses. Whole-head EEG was recorded while AWS (n = 20) and controls (n = 18) planned and executed spontaneous speech. Independent component analysis isolated clean bilateral mu components localized to sensorimotor cortices. Event-related PAC (ERPAC) was quantified using a Gaussian-copula mutual information estimator and cluster-based permutation testing. Across hemispheres, conditions, and trials, AWS exhibited reduced α–upper β coupling (25–32 Hz), suggesting reduced sensorimotor coordination. Within AWS, planning–execution ERPAC differences predicted stuttering frequency in opposing directions across hemispheres, with a left-hemisphere bias emerging as the strongest predictor (marginal R2 = 0.33, conditional R2 = 0.82). These findings suggest that α–β ERPAC is sensitive to oscillatory coordination…

title: Effect of Manure Cleaning Systems and Cleaning Frequency on Udder Hygiene Scores in Dairy Cattle
abstract: Hygiene is very important for food quality and animal welfare in the environmental surfaces of animal shelters. This study was conducted in 2023 across 10 large dairy farms located in Konya, Türkiye, to quantitatively determine the effects of manure scraper use on animal hygiene scores and barn cleanliness. The farms utilized three different manure cleaning systems: chain, steel rope, and hydraulic scrapers. Udder hygiene was scored on a 1–4 scale (1: clean, 2: slightly dirty, 3: moderately dirty, 4: very dirty/covered with manure). Contamination rates (%) on udders were determined using image processing technique. The effects of manure cleaning systems, stall material, and daily cleaning frequency on udder hygiene scores were evaluated. In addition, odor values were measured before and after cleaning in the farms. Data were analyzed using one-way ANOVA and correlation analysis. Animal udder contamination rates ranged between 4.45% and 13.8% across farms. It was determined that the daily manure cleaning frequency had a significant effect on the udder dirt rate (P

title: Artificial intelligence-supported learning and higher-order cognitive outcomes: the mediating role of metacognitive self-regulation
abstract: The growing adoption of AI in higher learning institutions poses important questions regarding its effects on higher-order cognitive competencies of students. Although previous studies have investigated perceptions of learning influenced by AI, very little information exists regarding the cognitive processes involved in AI interactions influencing learning performance. The present study sought to establish the relationship between AI task scaffolding, AI verification literacy, and cognitive offloading tendency in terms of their impacts on critical thinking and technical problem-solving of learners, with metacognitive self-regulation as the mediating factor. A cross-sectional design was employed using data from 533 university students across Ghana. Structural equation modeling (SEM) with bias-corrected bootstrapping in AMOS (version 23) was used to estimate the hypothesized relationships. The results indicate that AI task scaffolding is positively associated with both critical thinking and technical problem-solving, whereas cognitive offloading tendency is negatively associated with these outcomes. AI verification literacy does not directly predict the dependent variables but exerts indirect effects through metacognitive self-regulation. These results suggest that the educational value associated with AI-supported learning depends on how students engage with AI systems. The stud…

title: Inﬂuence of high-frequency electromagnetic ﬁeld-assisted TIG surface modiﬁcation on microstructural evolution, elemental redistribution and hardness of EN-GJV-400 compacted graphite iron
abstract: Introduction. Compacted graphite iron (EN-GJV-400) is widely used for highly loaded automotive and engineering components due to its favourable combination of strength, thermal conductivity, damping capacity and castability. However, the relatively moderate hardness and wear resistance of its surface region may limit its application under severe contact conditions. High-frequency electromagnetic field (HFEMF)-assisted treatment represents a potential approach for modifying solidification conditions and improving structural uniformity during surface engineering. Nevertheless, the influence of HFEMF-assisted TIG treatment on the microstructural evolution, elemental redistribution and hardness response of compacted graphite iron remains insufficiently understood. Materials and methods. In this study, conventional and HFEMF-assisted TIG surface modification of EN-GJV-400 compacted graphite iron was investigated. The experimental program included TIG remelting, TIG surface alloying using Ni78Si8B14 and CuSn-4 foils, and TIG hardfacing using UTP A DUR 600 chromium-containing filler wire, performed with and without electromagnetic assistance. A high-frequency electromagnetic field with a frequency of 200 kHz was applied during treatment. The modified surface layers were characterized using optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy combined with energy-dispersive X-ray spectrosc…

title: Frequency-specific resting-state EEG modulation during eyes-closed and eyes-open transitions in female soccer players
abstract: This study aimed to investigate differences in resting-state electroencephalographic (EEG) activity between female soccer players and female university students under eyes-open (EO) and eyes-closed (EC) conditions. A total of 25 female soccer players and 20 female university students participated in the study. Resting-state EEG signals were recorded using a 32-channel EEG system during 3 min of EO and 3 min of EC conditions. Absolute power in the delta (0.5–4 Hz), theta (4–8 Hz), alpha (8–13 Hz), and beta (13–30 Hz) frequency bands was calculated using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). Electrodes were grouped into four regions of interest (ROIs): frontal, central, parietal, and occipital regions. A three-way repeated-measures analysis of variance (Group × Condition × ROI) and difference-score analysis (Δ = EC – EO) were conducted to examine group differences. The results revealed significant main effects of Condition and ROI across all frequency bands (all p < 0.01), indicating that the EC–EO transition reliably modulated resting-state EEG activity. No significant group-related effects were observed in the alpha or theta bands (all p > 0.05). In contrast, a significant Condition × ROI × Group interaction was found in the beta band ( p < 0.05), whereas the delta band exhibited significant Condition × Group and Condition × ROI × Group interactions (both p < 0.05). Further…

title: Sleep fragmentation frequency is associated with distinct immune, microbial, and barrier-related profiles in DSS-induced colitis in mice
abstract: Background Sleep fragmentation is common in inflammatory bowel disease, but whether different fragmentation frequencies are associated with distinct biological responses during colitis remains unclear. This study examined endpoint-specific responses to low- and high-frequency sleep fragmentation in DSS-induced colitis in mice. Methods Male C57BL/6 mice were assigned to Control, DSS, DSS with low-frequency sleep fragmentation (DSS+LSF), DSS with high-frequency sleep fragmentation (DSS+HSF), or high-frequency sleep fragmentation alone (HSF). Colitis was induced with 2% DSS for 7 days. Sleep fragmentation was applied for 12 h/day during the light phase at 60 sweeps/h for LSF or 240 sweeps/h for HSF. Clinical indices, histology, epithelial barrier-associated proteins, inflammatory and stress-related markers, colonic CD4 + T-cell subsets, fecal microbiota composition, and fecal SCFAs were assessed. Results Clinical and macroscopic indices varied across experimental groups, but corrected comparisons among DSS-treated groups were not significant. Plasma corticosterone was increased in both DSS+LSF and DSS+HSF, whereas MPO was higher in DSS+LSF than in DSS+HSF. Colonic Th2 proportions were higher in DSS+HSF than in DSS and DSS+LSF. Other histological, barrier-associated, inflammatory, and metabolic findings were primarily descriptive. Conclusions Low- and high-frequency sleep fragmenta…

title: Dose-dependent power and connectivity modulation of low frequency oscillations through transcranial magnetic stimulation in non-human primates
abstract: Abstract Objective . Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is a powerful noninvasive tool for safely modulating neural activity in humans. In particular, the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) is a common target site for clinical interventions in disorders such as treatment-resistant depression. Yet, clinical trials investigating the efficacy of TMS often lack neural markers of target engagement of the DLPFC. Local field potentials (LFPs), such as prefrontal theta oscillations, have been implicated in the clinical symptoms of these disorders. However, noninvasive electroencephalography (EEG) recordings in humans are limited by their spatial resolution and challenges of interpreting EEG signals. Approach. In this study, we investigate the effects of single-pulse TMS applied to the left prefrontal cortex in non-human primates on LFPs recorded from intracranial stereo EEG electrodes. Main results. Compared to sham TMS, the intensity of active TMS pulses scaled with LFP power changes in a 1–13 Hz range at contacts close to the stimulation site in the prefrontal cortex (e.g. caudate nucleus, anterior cingulate cortex, insular cortex) as well as contacts that were more distal (e.g. posterior cingulate cortex, temporal lobe). To test how TMS modulates connectivity between these regions, we conducted a phase-based connectivity analysis. TMS pulses initially enhanced and then…

Frequency of depression and anxiety in patients with inborn errors of immunity: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background Inborn errors of immunity are chronic, genetically caused disorders that impair immune function and often increase susceptibility to infection. Many patients self-isolate because of infection-related concerns, which may increase the risk of mental health problems. This study evaluated symptoms of depression and anxiety and the need to address mental health in primary care. Methods In this cross-sectional study in Germany, fatigue, pain and quality of life were assessed using visual analogue scales. Routine clinical data including diagnosis, psychiatric comorbidities and susceptibility to infections were collected. Symptoms of depression and anxiety were evaluated using the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 questionnaires. Statistical analyses were performed to examine differences in self-isolation frequency and its association with pre-existing mental illness. Results A total of 143 patients (88 women and 55 men, mean age 45.4 years, range 21–85) were included. The median PHQ-9 score was 5 (IQR 8) and the median GAD-7 score was 5 (IQR 7). Eleven of 140 patients with PHQ-9 scores of at least 10 had no psychiatric diagnosis. Overall, 26% of patients with relevant symptoms had not received a diagnosis or treatment. Patients who self-isolated because of infection concerns had significantly higher PHQ-9 (Spearman’s ρ = 0.52, p < 0.001) and GAD-7 scores (Spearman’s ρ = 0.48, p < 0.…

title: Mechanism and therapeutic prospects of ferroptosis regulation through m6A in cancer
abstract: N6-methyladenosine (m6A), as the most abundant epitranscriptomic modification in eukaryotes, profoundly influences the metabolic fate of RNA. Meanwhile, ferroptosis, a regulated cell death modality driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation, has become a key component in tumor metabolic reprogramming. Increasing evidence suggests a deep interaction between m6A modification and ferroptosis, which plays a critical role in tumor occurrence and development, and treatment response. This review systematically elucidates the multidimensional regulatory mechanisms of m6A on ferroptosis regulatory factors, covering post-transcriptional modifications of the System Xc − /GSH/GPX4 antioxidant axis, iron metabolism-related proteins, and key enzymes of lipid peroxidation. It analyzes the dual role of the m6A-ferroptosis axis in tumor suppression and promotion, and then explores the function of this regulatory network in reshaping the tumor immune microenvironment and mediating treatment resistance. Finally, it looks forward to the translational potential of the m6A-ferroptosis interactive network as a novel biomarker and combination therapy target. Future research should integrate multi-omics and cutting-edge technologies to deeply analyze the spatiotemporal dynamic mechanism of this regulatory network in the occurrence and development of tumors, providing theoretical basis and new research…

title: Perceived government capacity and quality assurance effectiveness in higher education: evidence from Nangarhar, Afghanistan
abstract: Quality assurance in higher education is not just a technical process of assessing standards in the contemporary education system, but a governance process linked to the impact of government capacity, policy implementation, and institutional coordination. In Afghanistan, despite the existence of formal policies, standards, and evaluations for quality assurance, there is still a significant gap between these mechanisms and the actual quality of higher education. This study aims to assess the role of government capacity and institutional coordination in the effectiveness of quality assurance in higher education institutions in Nangarhar province. The study was conducted based on a quantitative, descriptive-analytical, and cross-sectional design. Data were collected from 240 selected participants through an online questionnaire from August 2025 to April 2026, from which 149 valid responses were received. Data analysis was conducted using SPSS, descriptive statistics, and a chi-square (χ²) test. The findings show that awareness of the importance of quality assurance is high (Mean=4.02), but policy clarity, trust, human capacity, professional training, financial support, and information systems are weak. A significant relationship was found between human capacity and quality assurance effectiveness (χ²=9.47, p=.003). Also, high institutional coherence is associated with high quality…

title: Baseline IFN-γ-based natural killer cell activity is associated with ex vivo expansion capacity of autologous NK cells in patients with breast cancer
abstract: Abstract Background Natural killer (NK) cell-based immunotherapy is increasingly explored in cancer treatment; however, inter-individual variability in NK cell expansion remains a major challenge. Clinically applicable biomarkers reflecting NK cell functional fitness prior to expansion are limited. Methods Peripheral blood samples from 33 patients with breast cancer were analyzed using a standardized whole-blood interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) release assay to assess baseline NK cell activity. NK cells were subsequently expanded ex vivo from peripheral blood mononuclear cells under cytokine-based culture conditions. Associations were evaluated using Spearman’s rank correlation. Results Baseline NK cell activity showed a significant positive correlation with NK cell expansion capacity ( r = 0.46, p = 0.007). In contrast, age, leukocyte counts, peripheral NK cell frequency, and initial NK cell number were not significantly associated with expansion outcomes. Conclusions Baseline IFN-γ-based NK cell activity is associated with the ex vivo expansion capacity of autologous NK cells and may serve as a candidate biomarker for predicting ex vivo NK-cell expansion and warrants validation in larger studies for optimizing NK cell-based immunotherapy strategies in patients with breast cancer.

WHO-ICOPE–Aligned Multidomain Interventions for Intrinsic Capacity in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: A Systematic Review of Randomised Controlled Trials
abstract: Background Intrinsic capacity (IC) reflects older adults’ physical and mental abilities, and its decline predicts loss of independence. The WHO Integrated Care for Older People (ICOPE) framework promotes multidomain, person-centred interventions, but evidence from trials remains limited. Objective To synthesise findings from randomised controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating WHO-ICOPE–aligned interventions in community-dwelling older adults. Methods Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines (PROSPERO CRD420250654375), five English-language RCTs published from January 2020 to December 2025 were included. Participants had decline in at least one IC domain. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, and findings were narratively synthesised due to heterogeneity. Results One trial implemented the full ICOPE pathway; four used partial approaches. Improvements were most consistent for locomotion and vitality, while cognitive and psychological findings varied and sensory effects were generally limited. No consistent advantage of full over partial implementation was established. Conclusions Evidence remains limited and heterogeneous; further high-quality trials are required.

title: Changes in Farmers’ Participation in Monitoring and Evaluation Following PMEL Capacity Building: Evidence from the Egerton University Agricultural Radio Program, Kenya
abstract: This study examined changes in farmers’ participation in monitoring and evaluation (M&E) following Participatory Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (PMEL) capacity building within the Egerton University Agricultural Radio Programme in Kenya. A one-group pretest–posttest design was used to assess changes in farmers’ participation before and after a six-month PMEL capacity-building intervention. The target population comprised 3,456 farmers and five key informants (KI), from whom 167 farmers and five key informants were selected. Quantitative data were collected using structured baseline and endline questionnaires, while focus group discussions and KI interviews provided qualitative contextual information. Farmer participation in M&E was measured using four Likert-type items assessing participation in agricultural programme meetings, provision of feedback, participation in monitoring activities, and participation in decision-making, rated on a five-point scale. The four items were combined into a composite participation score ranging from 1 to 5. PMEL capacity building involved participatory monitoring and evaluation concepts, feedback, reflection, learning, data collection and use of information for decision-making, delivered through radio-based interaction, review activities and three structured farm visits. Descriptive statistics and a paired-samples t-test were used for quan…

High-capacity multi-3D image watermarking using multidimensional multiplexing holography and QZ embedding
abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional (3D) images have become important information carriers in multimedia, medical treatment, and entertainment. However, existing 3D image hiding and watermarking schemes are mostly limited to single 3D image encryption, resulting in insufficient capacity, low security, and optimizable concealment. To address these issues, this paper proposes a high-capacity multi-3D image watermarking method based on multi-dimensional multiplexing holography and QZ embedding. Multiple 3D images are grouped and encoded into holographic watermarks using a multi-dimensional multiplexing hologram generation algorithm, where chaotic phase masks and spiral phase masks are adopted to expand the key space and enhance security. A contrast-guided embedding strategy is used to locate visually insensitive high-contrast regions in the two-dimensional host image, and the holographic watermarks are embedded into different wavelet sub-bands by combining discrete wavelet transform, singular value decomposition, and QZ embedding to achieve low distortion and strong robustness. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can simultaneously embed sixteen 3D images with high imperceptibility proved by ultrahigh correlation coefficient and negligible entropy variation, good key sensitivity, and reliable robustness against noise and occlusion attacks. title: Comparative Evaluation of Total Phenolic Content and Antioxidant Capacity in Aronia melanocarpa, Crataegus orientalis spp, and Cornus mas L. fruits
abstract: This study comparatively evaluated the total phenolic content (TPC) and antioxidant capacity of three phenolic-rich fruit species: Aronia melanocarpa (cv. Nero and Viking), Crataegus orientalis (hawthorn), and Cornus mas (cv. Yalçınkaya 77). Fully mature fruits were harvested during the 2024 growing season and analyzed using standardized Folin–Ciocalteu and ABTS assays. The experiment was conducted in a completely randomized design, and data were analyzed by analysis of variance (ANOVA) followed by LSD mean separation. Highly significant species effects were detected (p < 0.001). Aronia cultivars exhibited markedly higher phytochemical richness, with TPC values of 2594.44 mg GAE 100 g⁻¹ FW for cv. Viking and 2397.58 mg GAE 100 g⁻¹ FW for cv. Nero, clearly exceeding those of hawthorn (847.71 mg GAE 100 g⁻¹ FW) and cornelian cherry (821.45 mg GAE 100 g⁻¹ FW). Antioxidant capacity followed a similar pattern, with Viking (80.26%) and Nero (78.33%) showing significantly greater ABTS•⁺ radical-scavenging activity than hawthorn (49.28%) and cornelian cherry (51.60%). A strong linear relationship between TPC and antioxidant capacity (R2 = 0.9996) indicates that phenolic compounds are the principal contributors to antioxidant behavior across species. Overall, the results highlight the relatively higher antioxidant potential of A. melanocarpa and confirm hawthorn and cornelian cherry …

Good Agricultural Practices and Agricultural Marketing: A Province-Level Analysis of Production-Side Supply Capacity in Türkiye, 2025
abstract: This study compares the production-side supply capacity associated with Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) across Türkiye's 81 provinces and considers how this capacity may underpin agricultural marketing. The analysis uses the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry's 2025 provincial statistics on the number of GAP producers, production area, and crop output. In this cross-sectional and exploratory design, the three indicators were normalized to a 0–1 scale, given equal weights, and combined into the Good Agricultural Practices-Based Production-Side Supply Capacity Index (GAP-PSSCI; 0–100). Descriptive statistics included medians and interquartile ranges; both Pearson and Spearman correlations were calculated, and sensitivity to skewness was examined with a logarithmically transformed alternative index. Scores varied markedly across provinces: Adana ranked first (82.74), followed by Şanlıurfa (53.50), Konya (24.84), Gaziantep (21.64), and Mersin (11.90). title: Flash Loans and Market Volatility in DeFi: Evidence from a Time-Series Perspective
abstract: Collateral-free liquidity instantly conjured out of thin air. Flash loans have injected a strange, combustible brand of financial alchemy into decentralized finance, leaving risk managers and regulators sweating over market stability. We cornered this digital chaos using monthly time-series data alongside an ARDL bounds testing framework, tracking how these instantaneous fortunes warp price dynamics across Bitcoin and Ethereum markets. One size fits all? Absolutely not. Cross-asset heterogeneity is glaring: Bitcoin gets dragged into a prolonged, grinding dance with flash-loan-induced volatility, whereas Ethereum treats the shock like a brief, violent fever. This synthetic, protocol-based leverage inflates the DeFi ecosystem until price discovery breaks down. Yet, changing market regimes mutate these effects entirely, forcing a complete rethink of on-chain risk architecture..
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

Theoretical Analysis of Photon Detection Mechanism in Superconducting Single-Photon Detectors
abstract: To elucidate the photon detection mechanism of superconducting single-photon detectors, we theoretically examine the dynamics of type-II superconductors with a bias current using the two-dimensional time-dependent Ginzburg–Landau and the Maxwell equations. The photon injection that weakens the superconducting order parameter is treated phenomenologically as a local temperature increase, and the injected energy is controlled by the initial hotspot radius. The photon is detected by the voltage change between two electrodes attached to the left and right edges of the superconductor. We find that the detection dynamics in certain parameter ranges can be explained by the conventional hotspot model, whereas those in other parameter ranges are governed by the formation and subsequent dynamics of superconducting vortex and antivortex pairs. The photon detection is possible for an initial hotspot radius that exceeds a threshold value. We find that the generation of a vortex–antivortex pair occurs near the threshold. The flow of the pair perpendicular to the current direction finally creates a normal region for the photon detection. The voltage change for the Ginzburg–Landau parameter close to the transition point from type-II to type-I superconductor shows anomalous behavior that is not associated with the dynamics of the vortex–antivortex pair. title: Letter to the Editor: Beyond the mechanism: MiR-206 as a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in hepatocellular carcinoma after incomplete radiofrequency ablation
abstract: Lu et al in the World Journal of Gastrointestinal Oncology provided compelling evidence that micro RNA-206 (miR-206) suppressed hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence after incomplete radiofrequency ablation by targeting the hypoxia-inducible factor-1α and its downstream glycolytic target 6-phosphofructo-2-kinase/fructose-2,6-bisphosphatase 3. While the mechanistic insights provided are valuable, the clinical translational potential of miR-206 warrants greater emphasis, particularly given the current limitations of existing biomarkers, such as alpha-fetoprotein and protein induced by vitamin K absence or antagonist-II, which often lack sufficient sensitivity and specificity for predicting recurrence after ablation. We propose the translational potential may lie in exploring miRNA-206 as a dual-purpose tool: A preoperative prognostic biomarker for risk stratification and a post-ablation therapeutic agent delivered via advanced nanocarriers to the periablational zone. Future studies should investigate this potential duality to shift hepatocellular carcinoma management toward precision interventions.

title: Formation Mechanism of Corner Transverse Cracks in Heavy-section Gear Steel at Low Casting Speed and Optimization of Mold Flux
The Impact Mechanism of Unconscious Priming on Consumer Decision-Making: Cognitive Load as a Moderating Factor
abstract: From the last century to the present, whether consumer purchasing decisions are related to unconsciousness has always been a core issue. This article, as a literature review paper, systematically reviews the theoretical and empirical research on the relationship between unconscious priming, cognitive load, and consumer decision-making. The results of this review paper have found that unconscious priming mainly affects consumer decision-making through three pathways. High cognitive load enhances this effect through information presentation, product form, and the shopping platform environment, which decreases the ability to analyze rationally and then changes consumers' decision-making strategies. These findings indicate that the impact of unconscious priming on consumer decision-making is not determined by fixed factors alone but is also influenced by consumer cognitive load. This article not only represents theoretical contributions to the unconscious cognition of psychology, helping consumers better understand their own motivation, but also provides valuable strategic references for marketing practice, which helps to better understand consumer behavior and formulate more ethical strategies to improve the overall economy.

title: Integrated diagnostic model based on serum exosomal microRNAs and functional mechanism of miR-200b-3p in hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: BACKGROUND The early detection of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major clinical challenge due to the limited sensitivity and specificity of current biomarkers. This study sought to develop a diagnostic model based on serum exosomal microRNAs (miRNAs) and to elucidate the functional mechanism of a key miRNA, miR-200b-3p, in HCC pathogenesis. AIM To develop and validate a serum exosomal miRNA-based diagnostic model for HCC. METHODS Serum exosomes were isolated from a discovery cohort (68 HCC, 131 non-HCC) and a validation cohort (66 HCC, 135 non-HCC). Candidate miRNAs were identified via next-generation sequencing and machine learning, and validated by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. A diagnostic model was constructed using logistic regression. The role of miR-200b-3p was examined using in vitro functional assays. RESULTS A diagnostic model incorporating three exosomal miRNAs (miR-200b-3p, miR-215-5p, miR-452-5p) and age was established. It showed strong performance in the training set (area under the curve = 0.863, sensitivity = 86.4%, specificity = 76.5%; all P < 0.001). Mechanistically, miR-200b-3p acted as a tumor suppressor by directly targeting phosphoserine aminotransferase 1. Its overexpression inhibited HCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion (all P < 0.05), while knockdown promoted these phenotypes (all P < 0.05). CONCLUSION This stud…

title: Transcriptomics-based analysis of muscle injury mechanism mediated by inflammatory imbalance in the Duchenne muscular dystrophy muscle microenvironment
abstract: Background Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a hereditary neuromuscular disease characterized by progressive myofiber injury, chronic inflammatory response, and persistent fibrotic remodeling, for which no universal clinical treatment is currently available. The inflammatory-fibrotic microenvironment is regarded as a critical driver of DMD progression; nevertheless, the key molecules governing extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and immune imbalance remain incompletely elucidated. Methods Two transcriptomic datasets were integrated to construct an expression matrix containing DMD patients and healthy controls. Extracellular matrix (ECM) activation scores were calculated based on three representative ECM gene sets. Differential analysis combined with weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was performed to identify core modules related to DMD and ECM activation. A protein–protein interaction (PPI) network was built for the intersecting genes, and hub genes were screened by integrating five network topology algorithms. Immune cell infiltration characteristics were analyzed in protein tyrosine phosphatase receptor type C (PTPRC) high- and low-expression groups, followed by gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA). A PTPRC knockdown cell model was established, and quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR), Western blotting (WB), and immunofluorescence (IF) were applied to v…

title: Recent Advances in Antibiotic Degradation via Sulfate Radical Mediated AOPs: Bond Cleavage Mechanism, Fragmentation Pathways, and Interfacial Chemistry
abstract: Abstract Sulfate radical-based advanced oxidation processes (SR-AOPs) have emerged as promising and efficient technologies for the removal of antibiotics (ATBs) from aquatic environments due to their ability to generate highly reactive oxygen species and achieve effective contaminant degradation. The increasing persistence of ATBs in water bodies and their associated ecological and human health risks have stimulated extensive research on SR-AOP-based treatment strategies, including sulfate radical-driven oxidation, photocatalysis, electrochemical oxidation, sono-chemical processes, ozonation, and integrated hybrid systems. However, a comprehensive understanding of the molecular-level degradation mechanisms of ATBs, particularly the identification of reactive sites, bond cleavage pathways, and the roles of radical and non-radical reactive oxygen species (SO 4 •– / • OH/ O 2 •− / 1 O 2 ) remains insufficiently explored. This review provides a critical assessment of the sources, environmental occurrence, exposure pathways, and potential impacts of ATBs, along with existing regulatory frameworks for controlling antibiotic pollution. Furthermore, recent advances in SR-AOP strategies for ATB degradation are systematically discussed, with emphasis on reaction mechanisms, transformation products, structure reactivity relationships, and molecular fragmentation pathways. The review also …

title: Reaction mechanism and compressive strength of geopolymer based on the synergistic excitation of red mud and rice husk ash
abstract: The main purpose of this study is to take advantage of the synergetic effect of two solid wastes (red mud (RM) and rice husk ash (RHA)) and also solve the problem that RM alone has low activity and poor geopolymerization. Thus, geopolymer was made using RM as the main raw material, RHA as the siliceous activated agent, and NaOH-water glass mixed alkali activator. The effect of RHA on the compressive strength of geopolymer based on RM was studied. Combined with X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), and other test methods, the reaction mechanism of the synergistic activation of geopolymer was revealed. The results indicate that the mechanical properties of RM-based geopolymer are significantly enhanced by RHA addition. With 30% RHA, its compressive strength reaches 15.8 MPa in 60 days, representing a 327% increase over pure RM geopolymer (3.7 MPa). The synergistic system produces a product dominated by N-A-S-H gel with a minor amount of C-(N)-A-S-H gel, forming a three-dimensional polyaluminosilicate network that becomes denser with prolonged curing. These findings demonstrate that RM–RHA geopolymer has promising potential for practical applications such as road base materials, non-load-bearing wall panels, and industrial flooring, offering a sustainable solution for the large-scale utilization of these two solid wastes.

title: Atomic-Scale Mechanism of H2 Formation on Hydrated Olivine Surfaces
abstract: Abstract Abiotic hydrogen gas (H2) produced by the serpentinization of ultramafic rocks has far-reaching implications, from geological H2 production to the origin of life. In spite of this importance, the atomic-scale mechanism of H2 formation remains unclear. Here, we investigate H2 generation pathways on the hydrated olivine (010) surface using density functional theory (DFT+U) calculations with van der Waals corrections. Both the M1 and M2 surface terminations─formed by cleavage through the M1 or M2 metal ion sites, respectively─were examined, each containing isolated and paired Fe(II) ions. We find that isolated surface Fe(II) resists oxidation: while Fe(II) can transiently donate an electron to adsorbed H2O and induce reductive dissociation, the resulting charge-neutral H• is unstable and loses the electron upon hopping to a neighboring O site. The energy required for simultaneous formation of two H• radicals is also prohibitively high (∼3.5 eV), rendering H2 generation via the combination of two H• radicals unlikely. In contrast, paired Fe(II) at M1–M1 (adjacent ions on the M1 surface) and M1–M2 (cross-layer pairs) are prone to oxidation, forming a [Hδ+–Hδ–] reaction intermediate (a proton-hydride pair) that facilitates H2 generation. The rate-limiting step of the overall process is the reductive dissociation of H2O on surface Fe(II), with an activation energy of ∼1.9 eV.…

title: Research on Cloud Platform Based Spatial Resource Organization and Ownership Identification Mechanism for Generative Digital Theatre
abstract: This study develops a cloud-platform-based mechanism for organizing spatial resources and identifying ownership in generative digital theatre production. The research object includes stage-space layouts, virtual scene modules, lighting structures, prop models, background layers, and composite scenographic assets generated or edited during digital theatre creation. A dataset of 240 digital theatre spatial resources is constructed from 12 generative theatre scenes using Blender 4.0 and Unity 2022.3 LTS. Each asset package contains an FBX geometry file, PNG texture file, JPG preview, and JSON metadata record. Alibaba Cloud OSS is used for file storage, MongoDB 7.0 for scene-composition metadata, PostgreSQL 16 for ownership and reuse records, and Python 3.11 FastAPI for metadata registration and permission validation. Ownership identification combines creator ID, SHA-256 asset hash, creation timestamp, version number, and authorization status. Results show that the proposed mechanism achieves 0.964 ± 0.018*** classification accuracy, 142.6 ± 21.4 ms metadata retrieval time, 0.987 ± 0.009*** ownership verification accuracy, and 0.952 ± 0.016*** authorized reuse execution rate, supporting asset-level management of generative digital theatre resources.

title: The mechanism linking self-determined motivation to pickleball continuance intention: mediating role of leisure specialization and gender heterogeneity
abstract: Integrating Self-Determination Theory (SDT) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), this study examines how self-determined motivation (autonomy, competence, relatedness) shapes continuance intention among pickleball participants, with leisure specialization conceptualized as a domain-specific operationalization of perceived behavioral control (PBC). The mediating role of leisure specialization and the moderating effect of gender on the underlying motivational pathways are tested. Drawing on cross-sectional data from 789 Chinese tournament participants, structural equation modeling (SEM) reveals that all three dimensions of self-determined motivation exert significant positive effects on leisure specialization, which in turn partially mediates the relationship between self-determined motivation and continuance intention. Gender, however, does not significantly moderate the pathways linking motivational dimensions to leisure specialization, suggesting that the core motivational mechanism operates comparably across male and female participants. The findings provide empirical support for the pathway of “psychological need satisfaction → behavioral control (leisure specialization) → sustained participation,” and suggest that pickleball's low-skill-threshold design and mixed-gender format may help attenuate traditional gender-role barriers to sport participation. By validating thi…

title: The Mechanism of Visual Confinement and Affective Accumulation in the Cinematic Viewing Experience: An Analysis of the Film In the Mood for Love
abstract: Wong Kar-wai's In the Mood for Love is often discussed as a film about restrained love, nostalgia, and memory. Its emotional force comes less from direct confession or dramatic conflict than from the way the film makes desire difficult to see, approach, and complete. This paper adopts mise-en-scène as its main analytical framework to examine how the film turns unspoken love into a restricted viewing experience. In particular, it focuses on three formal mechanisms: confined space, obstructed framing, and repetitive temporal delay. Through these mechanisms, the paper argues that the film constructs an intimacy that is physically proximate yet emotionally inaccessible. First, narrow corridors, rented rooms, and staircases repeatedly bring Su Lizhen and Chow Mo-wan into close physical proximity, while the pressure of social visibility prevents their relationship from becoming openly expressed. Meanwhile, doorframes, windows, mirrors, and foreground objects interrupt the spectator's view, making the act of seeing incomplete and limited. Furthermore, recurring gestures, musical motifs, costumes, and encounters postpone narrative resolution, allowing emotions to accumulate gradually. Through these cinematic strategies, In the Mood for Love renders repression visual and temporal, leaving desire suspended in space, image, body, and memory.

title: The Brand Stickiness Mechanism of Uncertain Rewards: A Case Study of Mall Claw Machines
abstract: In experiential retail, uncertainty reward is becoming an important factor to promote consumption. This study takes the shopping mall claw machine as a case to analyze the psychological path of repeated consumption and the mechanism of establishing brand dependence. Qualitative methods were used to conduct in-depth interviews with 15 players to reveal their participation motivation and cognitive bias. The analysis shows that player behavior is mainly affected by the illusion of control and the near-cause winning effect. The former enables players to attribute random results to their own technology, while the latter enables near-misses to stimulate dopamine release and strengthen the urge to try again; these psychological effects are also enhanced by offline environment and onlooker factors. Studies have shown that brand stickiness depends on the behavior cycle driven by psychological expectations, rather than the product function itself; the research conclusions can provide reference for experiential business strategy design and consumer rights protection.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Wide-temperature-range tribological behavior and control mechanism of SnAg/ZrW 2 O 8 -incorporated Ni-based adaptive composite coatings
abstract: Abstract To realize the adaptive regulation of friction performance for core mechanical components over a wide temperature range, an integrated antifriction and wear-resistant composite structure combining coating, texture, and lubricant was proposed and prepared. Arrayed circular micropore textures were fabricated on CSS-42 L high-temperature bearing steel with a nickel-based hard coating, and SnAg soft metal lubricant doped with the negative thermal expansion agent ZrW2O8 was filled into the textures. Cellular automaton models were established to simulate the diffusion process of the lubricant, and combined with systematic tribological experiments, the frictional behavior and adaptive regulatory mechanism at different temperatures were systematically analyzed. Simulation results based on cellular automata models show that with increasing temperature, the proportion of medium- and high-concentration regions of SnAg lubricant increases gradually and reaches 75.28% at 350 °C, confirming the favorable diffusion behavior at elevated temperatures. Tribological tests reveal that the 95Sn5Ag-filled coating and the 95Sn5Ag–10 wt% ZrW2O8-filled coating exhibit significantly superior tribological properties compared with the pure Ni-based coating across a wide temperature range. At 350 °C, the average friction coefficients of the 95Sn5Ag-filled coating and the 95Sn5Ag–10 wt% ZrW2O8-fill…

title: Research on Artificial Aurora: Generation Mechanism, Technology and Application
abstract: Natural auroras are luminous plasma phenomena produced by collisions between solar wind charged particles and Earth's magnetosphere, while artificial auroras refer to controllable luminous phenomena simulated by human plasma technology. This paper sorts out three mainstream artificial aurora generation technologies: ionospheric heating, satellite electron beam injection and near-space plasma release. The study adopts case analysis and comparative analysis to compare the luminous scale, energy consumption and operation difficulty of the three technical routes, and systematically analyzes the scientific and engineering application values of artificial auroras, as well as potential ionospheric disturbance risks. The results show that ionospheric high-frequency heating is the most mature scheme for large-area artificial aurora with low energy cost but limited brightness; electron beam injection can form high-brightness aurora but has high launch cost; plasma balloon technology is low-cost and easy to implement yet only generates short-lived small-scale aurora. This research supplements horizontal comparative data of multiple artificial aurora technologies and provides reference for low-interference artificial aurora experiment design.

title: Analysis of Stock Price Driving Mechanism of Internet Media Based on LAD-Lasso
abstract: The extreme volatility and complex, multidimensional nature of the internet media sector often make traditional asset pricing models inadequate, prompting us to investigate Hong Kong-listed internet media companies to identify the actual driving forces behind their stock prices. To do this, we constructed a comprehensive dataset of 100 variables across five broad dimensions, including financial indicators and market signals; since real-world data typically contains significant noise, multicollinearity, and outliers, we introduced a Least Absolute Deviation penalized by Lasso (LAD-Lasso) model to handle these issues. This approach effectively blends absolute error loss with L1 regularization, making it possible to achieve robust parameter estimation and feature selection even when dealing with heavy-tailed distributions. Our empirical analysis shows that the LAD-Lasso model successfully shrinks the feature space down to 12 core variables with strong explanatory power. More importantly, compared to traditional OLS and standard Lasso models, the framework we propose delivers noticeably better overall performance, especially in maintaining consistent variable selection and keeping out-of-sample predictions stable. These results not only shed light on the underlying pricing mechanisms of internet media stocks, but they also provide a reliable statistical foundation for future corpor…

title: Evaluating and Comparing Wavelet Decomposition Models for Cotton (Gossypium spp.) Price Prediction in Andhra Pradesh, India
abstract: Cotton (Gossypium spp.) price forecasting is important for market decision-making in Andhra Pradesh, where price instability affects farmers, traders and related stakeholders. This study evaluated statistical, machine-learning and wavelet decomposition models for predicting monthly wholesale cotton prices in the Adoni market using secondary modal price data collected monthly from January 2010 to December 2024, comprising 180 observations. The period from January 2010 to December 2023 was used for model training, while January to December 2024 was retained for testing. The models compared were ARIMA (0,1,0), GARCH (1,1), ANN, Wavelet-ARIMA, Wavelet-ANN and Wavelet-GARCH. Forecasting performance was assessed using RMSE, MSE and MAPE, and residual diagnostics were used to examine model adequacy. The descriptive results indicated substantial variability in prices, with right-skewed price behaviour. Among the fitted models, GARCH (1,1) and ARIMA (0,1,0) produced the lowest training errors. In the test set, WANN recorded the lowest RMSE and MAPE, indicating strong out-of-sample predictive accuracy. However, the wavelet-based models showed residual autocorrelation. ARIMA demonstrated comparatively stable forecasting performance across training and testing, whereas ANN produced residuals without significant autocorrelation or nonlinear dependence. The findings indicate that model selec…

title: Do housing price cycles reflect herd behaviour in developing and emerging economies?
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether housing price cycles in 16 developing and emerging economies reflect herd behaviour. Design/methodology/approach This study used annual panel data from 2005 to 2023 sourced from the Bank for International Settlements and the World Bank’s World Development Indicators. The main model uses real housing price growth (inflation-adjusted) as the dependent variable and nominal housing price growth as a robustness check. Grounded in herd behaviour theory and information cascade theory, the study uses two-way fixed-effects panel regression, an instrumental-variables fixed-effects (FE-IV) estimator related to System GMM, and a mean group estimator, complemented by the Chang et al. (2000) cross-sectional absolute deviation (CSAD) herding test. Findings Macroeconomic fundamentals were found to be the dominant drivers of housing price growth, but the role of inflation shrinks sharply. In the preferred two-way fixed-effects specification, gross domestic product growth (β = 1.223, p < 0.01) is a robust predictor, while the coefficient of inflation falls from β = 1.816 (p < 0.01) under nominal growth to β = 0.388 (p = 0.015) under real growth, consistent with much of the previously observed inflation effect being mechanical rather than behavioural (R2 = 0.154 for real growth versus R2 = 0.444 for nominal growth in the same specification). title: Empirical Analysis of the Impact of Agricultural Enterprise Digitalization on Corporate Price Risk Exposure
abstract: This paper investigates whether digital transformation reduces the price risk exposure of agricultural enterprises. Agricultural firms are subject to pronounced seasonality, biological production cycles, weather shocks, product perishability, and frequent commodity price fluctuations, making their price risk more persistent than that of many manufacturing and service firms. Building on research into digital business strategy, smart farming, agricultural information systems, and financial risk exposure, this study constructs a panel data framework using Chinese A-share listed agricultural enterprises covering the period 2018–2022. Price risk exposure is measured as the sensitivity of firm value to changes in agricultural commodity prices. Digital transformation is primarily proxied by digital technology input scaled by total assets, and can be supplemented by a weighted digital transformation index when disaggregated indicators are available. Empirical evidence indicates that digitalization is significantly associated with lower price risk exposure: the standard deviation of product price fluctuations declines by 15.3%, the lag in market price transmission falls by approximately 23.7%, and highly digitalized firms record a 45.3% reduction in price risk exposure. This mitigating effect is stronger among firms with more complete digital systems and integrated operations covering p…
